LAW101.title: Introduction to Law
LAW101.description: Fundamental concepts. The relationship of law with political phenomena. The features of legal rules. The law and the sovereign relationship. Branches of law. Different legal systems. Turkish legal system and courts. Interpretation methods. Introduction to legal methodology.
LAW101.prerequisite: - LAW 101 Hukuka Giriş (Introduction to Law) (3+2+0) 3 AKTS 5 Temel kavramlar. Hukukun siyasi olgularla ilişkileri. Hukuk kurallarının özellikleri. Hukuk ve egemen ilişkisi. Hukukun dalları. Farklı hukuk sistemleri. Türk hukuk sistemi ve mahkemeler. Yorum metotları. Hukuk metodolojisine giriş.. Önkoşul: - 2- Hukuk Metodolojisi / Legal Methodology Ders kodu / Course code Ders adı / Course name Saat dağılımı / Credit hours BÜ kredisi/ BU credits AKTS / ECTS Önkoşul / Prerequisites Eşkoşul / Corequisite Not Tipi / Letter Grade Pass/Fail Dil / Language LAW 102 Hukuk Metodolojisi / Legal Methodology 3+2+0 3 5 - - Harf notu / Letter grade İngilizce / English

LAW102.title: Legal Methodology
LAW102.description: Legal theories and schools. Interpretation methods. The concept of analogy. The concept of legal gaps. Academic writing, referencing and academic presentation. Determining research topic and question, research plan. Resources in legal research. Doctrinal approach, comparative approach, historical approach, philosophical approach, socio-legal approach. Quantitative methods, qualitative methods. The relationship among method, argument, and pla
LAW102.prerequisite: - LAW 102 Hukuk Metodolojisi (Legal Methodology) (3+2+0) 3 AKTS 5 Hukuk teorileri ve okulları. Yorum metotları. Kıyas kavramı. Hukukta boşluk kavramı. Akademik yazım, atıf kuralları ve akademik sunum. Araştırma konusu ve sorusu belirleme, araştırma planı. Hukuk araştırmasında kullanılacak kaynaklar. Doktrinel yaklaşım, karşılaştırmalı yaklaşım, tarihsel yaklaşım, felsefi yaklaşım, sosyo-legal yaklaşım. Nicel yöntemler, nitel yöntemler. Metot, argüman ve plan arasındaki ilişki. Önkoşul: - 3- Anayasa Hukukunun Genel Esasları / General Principles of Constitutional Law Ders kodu / Course code Ders adı / Course name Saat dağılımı / Credit hours BÜ kredisi/ BU credits AKTS / ECTS Önkoşul / Prerequisites Eşkoşul / Corequisite Not Tipi / Letter Grade Pass/Fail Dil / Language LAW 103 Anayasa Hukukunun Genel Esasları / General Principles of Constitutional Law 3+2+0 3 5 - - Harf notu / Letter grade İngilizce / English

LAW103.title: General Principles of Constitutional Law
LAW103.description: The historical context and evolution of constitutional principles. Methods of constitutional interpretation and analysis. Basic doctrines concerning the structure of government and the protection of individual rights. Sources of constitutional law. Types of constitution. The constituent power. Sovereignty theories. Different organizational types of State. The political power and theories of legitimacy. Governmental systems. Democracy, electoral systems and political parties. Separation of powers; the legislative, executive, and judicial branches. Fundamental rights and freedoms. Constitutional jurisdiction.
LAW103.prerequisite: --- LAW 103 Anayasa Hukukunun Genel Esasları (General Principles of Constitutional Law) (3+2+0) 3 AKTS 5 Anayasal esasların tarihi bağlamı ve evrimi. Anayasal yorum ve analizin metotları. Bireysel hakların korunmasının ve devlet yapısının temel doktrinleri. Anayasal hukukunun kaynakları. Anayasa türleri. Kurucu iktidar. Egemenlik teorileri. Devletin farklı örgütlenme biçimleri. Siyasal iktidar ve meşruiyet teorileri. Hükümet sistemleri. Demokrasi, seçim sistemleri ve siyasi partiler. Kuvvetler ayrılığı; yasama, yürütme ve yargı organları. Temel hak ve hürriyetler. Anayasa yargısı. Önkoşul: -- 4- Türk Anayasa Hukuku ve Anayasa Yargısı / Turkish Constitutional Law and Judiciary Ders kodu / Course code Ders adı / Course name Saat dağılımı / Credit hours BÜ kredisi/ BU credits AKTS / ECTS Önkoşul / Prerequisites Eşkoşul / Corequisite Not Tipi / Letter Grade Pass/Fail Dil / Language LAW 104 Türk Anayasa Hukuku ve Yargısı / Turkish Constitutional Law and Judiciary 3+2+0 3 5 LAW 103 or consent of the instructor - Harf notu / Letter grade Türkçe / Turkish

LAW104.title: Turkish Constitutional Law and Judiciary
LAW104.description: The concept of constitution in Turkish constitutional law. Ottoman and Turkish constitutional developments. The 1982 Constitution: the fundamental principles in the Constitution and fundamental features of the State, fundamental rights and freedoms, the separation of powers in the Constitution. The legislature: the legal regime of political parties in Turkey. The executive: the regulatory acts of the executive. The judiciary: constitutionality review, the individual application, the decisions of the Constitutional Court.
LAW104.prerequisite: LAW 103 or consent of the instructor LAW 104 Türk Anayasa Hukuku ve Yargısı (Turkish Constitutional Law and Judiciary) (3+2+0) 3 AKTS 5 Türk Anayasa hukukunda anayasa kavramı. Osmanlı ve Türk anayasal gelişmeleri. 1982 Anayasası: Anayasa’daki temel ilkeler ve devletin temel nitelikleri, temel hak ve özgürlükler, Anayasa’da kuvvetler ayrılığı. Yasama: Türkiye’de siyasal partiler rejimi. Yürütme: yürütmenin düzenleyici işlemleri. Yargı: norm denetimi, bireysel başvuru, Anayasa Mahkemesi kararları. Önkoşul: LAW 103 veya öğretim elemanının onayı 5- Medeni Hukukun Temel Kavramları ve Kişiler Hukuku / Fundamental Terms of Civil Law and Law of Persons Ders kodu / Course code Ders adı / Course name Saat dağılımı / Credit hours BÜ kredisi/ BU credits AKTS / ECTS Önkoşul / Prerequisites Eşkoşul / Corequisite Not Tipi / Letter Grade Pass/Fail Dil / Language LAW 105 Medeni Hukukun Temel Kavramları ve Kişiler Hukuku / Fundamental Terms of Civil Law and Law of Persons 3+2+0 3 5 - - Harf notu / Letter grade Türkçe / Turkish

LAW105.title: Fundamental Terms of Civil Law and Law of Persons
LAW105.description: Etymology of civil law. Unwritten law and law created by judge. Concept of right. Legal transactions. Concepts of legal facts and acts. Bona fide, good faith, interdiction against abuse of rights. Commencement and end of personality of natural persons. Legal capacities. Registry of personal status. General principles of legal persons, associations, foundations.
LAW105.prerequisite: - LAW 105 Medeni Hukukun Temel Kavramları ve Kişiler Hukuku (Fundamental Terms of Civil Law and Law of Persons) (3+2+0) 3 AKTS 5 Medeni hukukun etimolojisi. Yazılı olmayan ve hakim tarafından yaratılan hukuk. Hak kavramı. Hukuki işlemler. Hukuki olay ve fiil kavramları. İyi niyet, dürüstlük kuralı, hakkın kötüye kullanılması yasağı. Gerçek kişilerde kişiliğin başlangıcı ve sona ermesi. Kişinin ehliyetleri. Kişisel durum sicilleri. Tüzel kişilere ilişkin genel esaslar, dernekler, vakıflar. Önkoşul: - 6- Aile Hukuku / Family Law Ders kodu / Course code Ders adı / Course name Saat dağılımı / Credit hours BÜ kredisi/ BU credits AKTS / ECTS Önkoşul / Prerequisites Eşkoşul / Corequisite Not Tipi / Letter Grade Pass/Fail Dil / Language LAW 106 Aile Hukuku / Family Law 3+2+0 3 5 - - Harf notu / Letter grade Türkçe / Turkish

LAW106.title: Family Law
LAW106.description: Betrothal. Legal nature and formal requirements of marriage. Voidness of marriage, ipso facto dissolution of marriage. Divorce, separation. General terms of marital union, protection of marital union, marital property regimes. Establishment and terms of paternity. Adoption. Administration of family relations. Guardianship.
LAW106.prerequisite: - LAW 106 Aile Hukuku (Family Law) (3+2+0) 3 AKTS 5 Nişanlanma. Evlenmenin hukuki niteliği ve evlenmede şekil şartları. Evlenmenin hükümsüzlüğü, evliliğin kendiliğinden sona ermesi. Boşanma, ayrılık. Evlilik birliğinin genel hükümleri, evlilik birliğinin korunması, mal rejimleri. Soybağının kurulması ve hükümleri. Evlat edinme. Aile topluluğunun idaresi. Vesayet. Önkoşul: - 7- Borçlar Hukuku I (Genel Hükümler) / Law of Obligations I (General Provisions) Ders kodu / Course code Ders adı / Course name Saat dağılımı / Credit hours BÜ kredisi/ BU credits AKTS / ECTS Önkoşul / Prerequisites Eşkoşul / Corequisite Not Tipi / Letter Grade Pass/Fail Dil / Language LAW 201 Borçlar Hukuku I (Genel Hükümler ) / Law of Obligations I (General Provisions ) 3+2+0 3 5 - - Harf notu / Letter grade Türkçe / Turkish

LAW201.title: Law of Obligations I (General Provisions )
LAW201.description: Characteristics of obligatory relations. Sources of obligations. Formation and types of contracts. Standard terms. Obligation to contract. Interpretation and completion of contracts. Revision of contracts. Validity of contracts. Concept of simulated contract. Abstract acknowledgement of debt. Agency. Tort. Determination of material and immaterial damages. Strict liability.
LAW201.prerequisite: - LAW 201 Borçlar Hukuku I (Genel Hükümler ) (Law of Obligations I (General Provisions )) (3+2+0) 3 AKTS 5 Borç ilişkisinin niteliği. Borçların kaynakları. Sözleşmelerin kurulması ve türleri. Genel işlem koşulları. Sözleşme yapma zorunluluğu. Sözleşmelerin yorumlanması ve tamamlanması. Sözleşmelerin uyarlanması. Sözleşmelerin geçerliliği. Muvazaa kavramı. Soyut borç ikrarı. Temsil. Haksız fiiller. Maddi ve manevi zararın belirlenmesi. Kusursuz sorumluluk. Önkoşul: - 8- Borçlar Hukuku II (Genel Hükümler ) / Law of Obligations II (General Provisions ) Ders kodu / Course code Ders adı / Course name Saat dağılımı / Credit hours BÜ kredisi/ BU credits AKTS / ECTS Önkoşul / Prerequisites Eşkoşul / Corequisite Not Tipi / Letter Grade Pass/Fail Dil / Language LAW 202 Borçlar Hukuku II (Genel Hükümler) / Law of Obligations II (General Provisions ) 3+2+0 3 5 - - Harf notu / Letter grade Türkçe / Turkish

LAW202.title: Law of Obligations II (General Provisions )
LAW202.description: Performance of obligations. Default of creditor, default of debtor. Non-performance of obligations. Specific performance. Action for damages. Extinguishment of obligations. Limitation period. Conditional obligations. Contract conferring rights to a third party. Unjust enrichment. Assignment of claims, assumption of obligations. Joint and several liability.
LAW202.prerequisite: - LAW 202 Borçlar Hukuku II (Genel Hükümler ) (Law of Obligations II (General Provisions )) (3+2+0) 3 AKTS 5 Borçların ifası. Alacaklı temerrüdü, borçlu temerrüdü. Borcun ifa edilmemesi. İfa davası. Tazminat davası. Borçların sona ermesi. Zamanaşımı. Koşula bağlı borçlar. Üçüncü kişi yararına sözleşme. Sebepsiz zenginleşme. Alacağın temliki, borcun nakli. Teselsül. LAW203.title: Criminal Law I (General Provisions)
LAW203.description: Fundamental concepts. Historical analysis. Distinctive features of criminal law. Legitimacy of the punitive power. Normative sources and their interpretation. The field of application of criminal norms. General theory of crime. Matters outside the elements of crime. Elements of crime in different systems.
LAW203.prerequisite: - LAW 203 Ceza Hukuku I (Genel Hükümler) (Criminal Law I (General Provisions)) (3+2+0) 3 AKTS 5 Temel kavramlar. Tarihsel analiz. Ceza hukukunun ayırt edici özellikleri. Cezalandırma yetkisinin meşruiyeti. Normatif kaynaklar ve bunların yorumu. Ceza kanunlarının uygulama alanı. Suç genel teorisi. Suçun unsurları dışında kalan hususlar. Farklı sistemlerde suçun unsurları. Önkoşul: - 10- Ceza Hukuku II (Genel Hükümler) / Criminal Law II (General Provisions) Ders kodu / Course code Ders adı / Course name Saat dağılımı / Credit hours BÜ kredisi/ BU credits AKTS / ECTS Önkoşul / Prerequisites Eşkoşul / Corequisite Not Tipi / Letter Grade Pass/Fail Dil / Language LAW 204 Ceza Hukuku II (Genel Hükümler) / Criminal Law II (General Provisions) 3+2+0 3 5 - - Harf notu / Letter grade Türkçe / Turkish

LAW204.title: Criminal Law II (General Provisions)
LAW204.description: Typical action, illegality, culpability. Attempt, complicity, aggregation. Penalty and security measures. Determination of the penalty. Termination of penal relationship.
LAW204.prerequisite: - LAW 204 Ceza Hukuku II (Genel Hükümler) (Criminal Law II (General Provisions)) (3+2+0) 3 AKTS 5 Tipe uygun fiil, hukuka aykırılık, kusurluluk. Teşebbüs, iştirak, içtima. Cezalar ve güvenlik tedbirleri. Cezanın belirlenmesi. Ceza ilişkisinin düşmesi. Önkoşul: - 11- İdare Hukuku I / Administrative Law I Ders kodu / Course code Ders adı / Course name Saat dağılımı / Credit hours BÜ kredisi/ BU credits AKTS / ECTS Önkoşul / Prerequisites Eşkoşul / Corequisite Not Tipi / Letter Grade Pass/Fail Dil / Language LAW 205 İdare Hukuku I / Administrative Law I 3+2+0 3 5 - - Harf notu / Letter grade Türkçe / Turkish

LAW205.title: Administrative Law I
LAW205.description: Administrative state. Administrative law and individual rights. Public legal entity. Administrative hierarchy and administrative tutelage. Administrative organisation. The legal structure of the public service. The principles of public service. The personnel of public service. The property of public service. The fulfilment methods of the public service: privatisation, law enforcement. Methods of acquiring properties by the administration.
LAW205.prerequisite: - LAW 205 İdare Hukuku I (Administrative Law I) (3+2+0) 3 AKTS 5 İdari rejim. İdare hukuku ve bireysel haklar. Kamu tüzel kişiliği. İdari hiyerarşi ve idari vesayet. İdari teşkilatlanma. Kamu hizmetinin hukuki yapısı. Kamu hizmetinin ilkeleri. Kamu hizmetinin personeli. Kamu hizmetinin eşyası. Kamu hizmetinin görülme usulleri: özelleştirme, kolluk. İdarenin mal edinme usulleri. LAW206.title: Administrative Law II
LAW206.description: The individual administrative acts of the administration. The regulatory acts of administration. The administrative contracts. The legal characteristics of the administrative sanctions, the regulatory administrative sanctions, financial administrative sanctions. The liability of the administration. The supervision over the administration by non-judicial methods. The supervision over the administration by judicial methods. The legal remedies in the administrative judiciary. Administrative procedure and its principles. Administrative actions. The execution of the judgments in administrative judiciary.
LAW206.prerequisite: - LAW 206 İdare Hukuku II (Administrative Law II) (3+2+0) 3 AKTS 5 İdarenin bireysel idari işlemleri. İdarenin düzenleyici işlemleri. İdari sözleşmeler. İdari yaptırımların hukuki niteliği, düzenleyici idari yaptırımlar, mali idari yaptırımlar. İdarenin sorumluluğu. İdarenin yargı-dışı yollardan denetimi. İdarenin yargısal denetimi. İdari yargıda kanun yolları. İdari yargılama usulü ve ilkeleri. İdari davalar. İdari yargıda kararların uygulanması. The development of constitutional politics in Türkiye from the Ottoman Empire to present. Constitutional changes from the 1876 Kanun-ı Esasi to the 1921, 1924, 1961, and 1982 Constitutions, and the transition from a parliamentary to a presidential system. Balance of power between the legislative, executive, and judicial branches. The role of the Constitutional Court and judicial review. Fundamental rights, and emergency regimes. (Taught in Turkish)

Yasama, yürütme ve yargı erkleri arasındaki güç dengeleri. Anayasa mahkemesi ve yargısal denetim. Temel haklar ve olağanüstü hâl rejimleri. Legal protection mechanisms including non-disclosure agreements, confidentiality clauses, and exclusivity provisions. Intellectual property protection in business contexts. Commercial relationships including agency, distribution, franchising, and licensing agreements. Contract drafting, legal formalities, and practical aspects of business law for legal professionals.

Gizlilik ve ifşa etmeme anlaşmaları, gizlilik maddeleri ve münhasırlık hükümleri dahil yasal koruma mekanizmaları. İş bağlamında fikri mülkiyet koruması. Social and environmental public policy. The organisational, technical, and legal barriers to policy innovation.

Patent registration. Inventorship and patent ownership. Scope of patent protection and patent infringement. Definition and elements of work. Types of works: scientific

and literary works, musical works, cinematographic works and works of fine arts. Authorship. Economic and moral rights of authors. Related rights, exceptions and limitations.

Markanın fonksiyonları ve ekonomik analizi. Marka türleri. Marka tescil prosedürü. Mutlak ve nispi ret nedenleri. Marka korumasının kapsamı ve marka hakkına tecavüz. Hükümsüzlük ve iptal. Buluş ve patent hakkı sahipliği. Patent korumasının kapsamı ve patent hakkının ihlali. Eser tanımı ve unsurları. Criminal procedure in the Anglo-Saxon system. Unification of criminal law. European Criminal Law norms established by the European Court of Human Rights. Influence of the European Union on the evolution of the criminal law systems of the Member States.

Contemporary challenges in international economic law: digital trade, rising protectionism, role of AI, corporate social responsibility.

Ekonomik etkinlik ve dışsallık kavramları. Hukukun oluşum süreçleri. Liberal ekonomi ve regülasyon ilişkisi. Düzenleme yöntemleri. Mülkiyetin ekonomik analizi. Haksız fiilin ekonomik analizi. Sözleşme hukukunun ekonomik analizi. Aile hukukunun ekonomik analizi. Ceza hukukunun ekonomik analizi. Hukuksal süreçlerin ekonomik analizi. Güncel hukuki sorunların ekonomik analizi. LAW441.title: Alternative Dispute Resolution
LAW441.description: Conflicts, disputes and dispute resolution. The concept and function of Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR). ADR in comparative law. Main methods of ADR. Negotiations and round table discussions. Mediation. Mandatory mediation. Mediation-arbitration (Med-Arb). Arbitration. Online dispute resolution. Blockchain based dispute resolution.
LAW441.prerequisite: - LAW 441 Alternatif Uyuşmazlık Çözümü (Alternative Dispute Resolution) (3+2+0) 3 AKTS 5 Çatışmalar, uyuşmazlıklar ve uyuşmazlık çözümü. Alternatif Uyuşmazlık Çözümü (ADR) kavramı ve işlevi. Karşılaştırmalı hukukta ADR. ADR'nin temel yöntemleri. Müzakereler ve yuvarlak masa tartışmaları. Arabuluculuk. Zorunlu arabuluculuk. Arabuluculuk-tahkim. Tahkim. Çevrimiçi uyuşmazlık çözümü. Blokzincir tabanlı uyuşmazlık çözümü. LAW443.title: Electronic Commerce Law
LAW443.description: The concept of e-commerce and the scope of e-commerce law. Development and functioning of e-commerce market. Service provider. Intermediary service provider. E-commerce marketplace. Commercial electronic message.

LAW444.title: Immigration and Citizenship Law
LAW444.description:
General principles of immigration law. Foreigners’ entry, residence and travel in Türkiye. The rights and freedoms of foreigners. Foreigners and human rights law. Deportation and the principle of non-refoulement. Right to work. Right to acquire immovable property. Investment of foreigners. Introduction to citizenship law. Principles of citizenship law. Introduction to Turkish citizenship law. Acquisition of citizenship. Loss of citizenship. Proof of citizenship. Disputes in citizenship and settlement methods. Prerequisite: --

Türk vatandaşlık hukukuna giriş. Vatandaşlığın kazanılması. Vatandaşlığın kaybı. Vatandaşlığın ispatı. Vatandaşlık ihtilafları ve çözüm yolları.

LAW446.title: Legal Clinic
LAW446.description: Practical legal education methods. Legal presentation techniques. Developing and discussing projects to strengthen access to justice for disadvantaged groups. Providing legal support to individuals regarding access to justice, under the supervision of the faculty member and through consultations with legal practitioners. Conducting public outreach activities related to the legal and justice system. Providing legal training for non-lawyers and high school students or equivalent and reporting the outcomes of these efforts.

EC101.title: Principles of Microeconomics
EC101.description: Nature, scope and methods of economics; a general view of the price system; consumer behavior; theory of the firm; illustrations and applications from the Turkish economy.

EC102.title: Principles of Macroeconomic
EC102.description: National income and its determination; changes in national income, elements of public finance, money and banking, international trade, macroeconomic policy, economic growth and development; illustrations and applications from the Turkish economy.

EC103.title: Orientation to Economics I
EC103.description: A short history of economics, its development, its present status, and its contribution to other social sciences; issues pertaining to positive versus normative economics, macro- versus micro-economics.

EC104.title: Orientation to Economics II
EC104.description: Presentation of different areas of research in economics and curriculum offerings related to them; overview of helpful resources for theoretical and applied research in economics.

EC203.title: Microeconomics I
EC203.description: Consumer theory, budget constraint, utility maximization, individual demand, income and substitution effects; market demand; firm theory, profit maximization, cost minimization; firm supply; market supply; general equilibrium; consumer and producer surplus; Walrasian equilibrium; efficiency and equilibrium; welfare theorems; monopoly; market failures.

EC205.title: Macroeconomics I
EC205.description: Classical and monetarist economic theories; exogenous economic growth models; economic fluctuations and Keynesian short-run economic models; the Lucas critique and theory of rational expectations; life-cycle permanent income hypothesis and the real business cycle theory.

EC206.title: Microeconomics II
EC206.description: Public goods; externalities; inefficiency in monopoly; price discrimination; policy, regulation and role of government; oligopoly. Static games under complete information: dominated strategies, Nash equilibrium. Dynamic games: backward induction; subgame perfect equilibrium; repeated games. Information economics: decision under uncertainty; adverse selection; moral hazard.

EC208.title: Macroeconomics II
EC208.description: Open economy macroeconomics: exchange rate regimes; Mundell-Fleming and Dornbush models; monetary, fiscal and exchange rate policies; foreign exchange markets; international trade and finance in small open economies. Global imbalances; currency crisis; twin-deficits; balance of payments adjustments; domestic and foreign savings and economic growth in open economies.

EC223.title: Mathematics for Economists
EC223.description: Fundamental logic; set theory; relations; functions; limits, continuity and differentiability; univariate-multivariate calculus; static optimization; Lagrange and Kuhn-Tucker theorems; difference equations; differential equations; phase diagrams; dynamic optimization. Economic applications.

EC233.title: Mathematical Statistics I
EC233.description: Introduction to statistics; data presentation with graphical and numerical methods; probability theory; conditional probability; discrete and continuous random variables and their probability distributions; multivariate probability distributions. Data applications.

EC234.title: Mathematical Statistics II
EC234.description: Elements of statistical analysis; sampling distributions and the central limit theorem; statistical inference including estimation and tests of hypotheses. Data applications.

EC301.title: Economics of Industrial Organization
EC301.description: Review of firm theory; economies and scale; monopoly and market power; durable good monopoly; price discrimination; nonlinear pricing; twopart tariff; bundling and tying; Dixit’s entry deterrence model; theories of competition; oligopoly; monopolistic competition; product differentiation; Hotelling’s location model; mergers; collusions; price competition under demand shocks; quality signaling; technological progress; R&D and patents. Industry case studies.

EC304.title: Game Theory
EC304.description: Dominance, iterated elimination of dominated strategies; best response and Nash equilibrium; rationalizability; undominated Nash equilibrium; mixed strategy Nash equilibrium; Bayesian Nash equilibrium; backward induction; subgame perfect Nash equilibrium; perfect Bayesian equilibrium; signaling games; repeated games; other refinements. Applications: auctions; bargaining; voting.

EC305.title: Urban Economics
EC305.description: Economic analysis as applied to urban problems and policy; the need for cities; urban spatial structure; urban transportation; housing; local public goods.

EC306.title: Advanced Microeconomics
EC306.description: Information economics: strategic interaction under asymmetric information; moral hazard (hidden action); adverse selection (hidden information). Selected applications: principal-agent models, bargaining, auctions, insurance markets, labor markets, herd behavior, voting. Experimental economics; behavioral economics.

EC307.title: Evolution of Economies and Economics
EC307.description: A review of evolution of economic institutions in history; development of economic thinking in the context of changing economic environment; alternative paradigms for analyzing economic issues and policies.

EC308.title: Advanced Macroeconomics
EC308.description: Dynamic models in macroeconomics; calculus of variations; optimal control and dynamic programming methods; general equilibrium theory; applications in economic growth; real business cycles and political economy.

EC310.title: Economic History of Europe
EC310.description: Introduction to the economy history of Europe; a survey of economic and social characteristics of different periods; Medieval, Early Modern and Modern Periods; factors driving economic and social change.

EC311.title: Economic History of the Ottoman Empire
EC311.description: Introduction to Ottoman economic history; review of evidence on different periods of the Ottoman history; institutions and institutional change; causes of economic stagnation; comparative analysis with other regions of the world.

EC312.title: Comparative Schools of Thought in Economics
EC312.description: The subject matter and methodological standpoint of leading traditions of economic thought: Neoclassical, Keynesian, Post Keynesian, Chicago, Austrian, Institutional, Marxian, Feminist and Radical.

EC314.title: Economic Methodology and Philosophy of Economics
EC314.description: Economics as a science; methodologies of and epistemologies in economics; logical positivism, falsificationism, research programs, scientific paradigms and epistemological anarchism; methodological debates and innovations in economics.

EC315.title: Economic History of Turkey
EC315.description: The economic and social history of the 19th and 20th century Turkey; economic policy in different periods; changing social coalitions and conflict; economic growth and distribution over time; interaction with the outside world.

EC317.title: Gender and the Economy
EC317.description: Understanding of gender roles in the household, the labor market, and the firm; feminist economic critique of mainstream economics and alternatives; gender division of labor; paid and unpaid work; occupational segregation and discrimination; economic and social policies altering or reinforcing prevailing gender roles.

EC331.title: Econometrics
EC331.description: Classical least squares analysis; properties of least squares estimators; statistical inference in simple and multiple regression; misspecification problem; regression with dummy variables.

EC332.title: Advanced Econometrics
EC332.description: Heteroskedasticity; autocorrelated errors; univariate and multivariate time-series analysis; time varying volatility models; simultaneous equation models; system methods of estimation; limited dependent variables, instrumental variables.

EC344.title: Money, Banking and Financial Institutions
EC344.description: Bond markets and yield to maturity; determinants of interest rates; risk and term structure of interest rates; stock markets, risk-return theories, and efficient market hypothesis; derivative assets and hedging; roles of financial intermediaries, bank management, banking regulations; financial crises; central banking, conduct of monetary policy and monetary base; money supply process and monetary policy tools.

EC350.title: Government Control
EC350.description: Structure of markets; promotion of competition by anti-trust laws and other means; public control of certain industries, including public utility regulation; government control of production, sales and prices, government ownership and operations.

EC351.title: Public Finance
EC351.description: Causes of market failure and the need for government intervention in the economy (analysis of public goods, externalities, decreasing cost conditions); the problem of income distribution; budget systems and cost-benefit analysis; government expenditure patterns and tax structures.

EC352.title: Topics in Public Finance
EC352.description: Theory of income determination; unemployment problems; the theory of economic stabilization and the impact of government expenditures and taxes on the level of economic activity.

EC358.title: World Economic History
EC358.description: Survey of world economic history; theories of long run economic development; discussion of roles of geography, institutions, politics and culture; characteristics of and empirical evidence on different eras; transition to agriculture; Malthusian era; industrialization.

EC361.title: International Economics
EC361.description: The determinants of international trade, patterns of specialization and gains from trade in classical and neoclassical (Ricardian, Hecksher-OhlinSamuelson) models and new trade theories; effects of trade on production and consumption patterns, factor prices, income distribution, economic growth and development; instruments and effectiveness of trade policy.

EC362.title: Topics in International Economics
EC362.description: Theory and practice of international macroeconomics and finance; balance of payments, adjustment mechanisms, functioning of foreign exchange markets and international capital markets; global economic and financial interactions and international policy coordination; financial crises and contagion.

EC403.title: Economic Policy
EC403.description: Growth and development policy; fiscal policy; monetary policy; labor market policy; open economy and trade issues; political economy of economic policy; redistribution, government regulation and oversight; political aspects of economic policy-making.

EC404.title: Environmental and Ecological Economics
EC404.description: The development of environmental thinking in economics; alternative definitions and measurements of sustainability; a survey of contemporary economic approaches that conceptualize the economics-environment relationship; environmental valuation; decision-making techniques, costbenefit analysis and multi-criteria evaluation; environmental policy instruments. Case studies.

EC405.title: Transportation Economics
EC405.description: Nature of demand and cost in the transportation industry; pricing of transportation services; resource allocation; urban transportation; problems of congestion; transportation and location theory; international transportation organizations.

EC406.title: Agricultural Economics
EC406.description: Sources and nature of contemporary agricultural problems; various models of agricultural development: the role and effect of agricultural policies; the interrelationships between agricultural development and other sectors of the economy; analysis of food systems; impacts of technology use in agriculture; applications to agribusiness; Turkish agricultural problems and various possible methods of solving these problems.

EC407.title: Labor Economics
EC407.description: Determinants of labor supply and labor demand; determinants of wages; welfare programs and work incentives; household production; the employment effects of minimum wages; the impact of immigration on the wage and employment opportunities of natives; segmentation and discrimination in labor markets; human capital investment; estimating the rate of return on schooling; impact of government programs on labor market outcomes.

EC408.title: Applied Macroeconomics
EC408.description: Macroeconomics from an applied perspective; national income accounting; applied general equilibrium; calibration and simulation; economic growth—the roles of capital accumulation, increased education, and technological progress in determining economic growth; savings—the effect of government and private debt on economic growth; and exchange-rate regimes.

EC409.title: Health Economics
EC409.description: The supply and demand for health services; health insurance, adverse selection, moral hazard; healthcare providers, physicians, hospitals, pharmaceuticals; health systems, regulation, financing of health care and health care reform.

EC411.title: History of Economic Thought
EC411.description: The pre-history of classical political economy; forefathers and constitutive debates in the classical political economy. Marx’s challenge and critique; transition from feudalism to capitalism; colonialism; enclosure movement; industrial revolution; the free trade debate; population growth; capitalism and its crises.
EC411.prerequisite: EC 203, EC 205; or consent of the instructor.

EC412.title: Topics in History of Economic Thought
EC412.description: Constitutive debates and internal divisions in neoclassical economics; the heterodox alternatives to the neoclassical orthodoxy; different notions of actors, knowledge and equilibrium; different explanations of the interactions between markets and states; different theories of market and government failures; different and competing conceptualizations of the role that institutions, power mechanisms and class structures play in shaping social outcomes.

EC414.title: Institutional Economics
EC414.description: Introduction to institutional economics; definitions, key concepts and methodology of institutional economics; examples of economic institutions in historical developments; evolution of economic and political organizations, laws, contracts and customs in different regions; game theoretic models and empirical studies.

EC416.title: Marxian Economics
EC416.description: Introduction to Marxian economics; definitions, key concepts and methodology of Marxian economics; modes of production; transition from feudalism to capitalism; labor theory of value; class analysis; capitalism and its crisis tendencies.

EC419.title: Mechanism Design
EC419.description: Impossibility theorems; implementation; direct mechanisms; the revelation principle; Vickrey-Clarke-Groves (VCG) mechanisms; Arrowd'Aspremont-Gerard-Varet (AAGV) mechanisms; auctions with private values; first-price auctions; second-price auctions; revenue equivalence; optimal auctions; auctions with interdependent values; winner’s curse; affiliation; English auction; linkage principle.

EC423.title: Economics of Corporate Finance
EC423.description: Tools and techniques of corporate finance, with emphasis on theoretical foundations; economic analysis of investment, financing, capital structure, and dividend policy decisions of firms and corporations.

EC425.title: Diverse Economies
EC425.description: Alternative ways of conceptualizing economies and organizing economic processes. Alternative ways of conceptualizing economies: diverse economies framework with special emphasis on household economies, gift economies, sustainable economies, communal economies, cooperative economies and participative economies. Alternative ways of organizing economic processes: controlling markets, extending credit, taming capital and building community and solidarity economies.

EC427.title: Financial Economics I
EC427.description: Theory of financial economics: analysis of financial decision making; portfolio theory; asset pricing theory; arbitrage theory and efficient market hypothesis.

EC428.title: Financial Economics II
EC428.description: Theory and applications of the term structure of interest rates, derivatives, futures and options markets, volatility models.

EC431.title: Applied Econometrics I
EC431.description: Examination of the problems of micro-econometric model building; testing; preparing and analyzing forecasts; discrete choice models; panel data estimation with micro-econometric data; simultaneous equations.

EC432.title: Applied Econometrics II
EC432.description: Examination of macro-econometric models; estimation, forecasting and simulation; introduction to large sample theory; panel data estimation with macro-econometric data.

EC433.title: Project Evaluation
EC433.description: A critical survey of general investment criteria, Social Marginal Productivity of Capital (SMP), marginal per capita reinvestment surplus and time series criteria; the Little-Mirrlees method of project appraisal: choice of a numeraire and world prices; valuation of traded and non-traded goods, shadow wages and accounting rate of interest. The UNIDO approach to project appraisal: direct present benefits and costs, indirect future benefits and costs, the shadow wage rates, shadow price of investment and social discount rate, project appraisal and income distribution.

EC436.title: Quantitative Methods for Public Policy Evaluation
EC436.description: Causality versus correlation; descriptive analysis; randomized experiment; natural experiments and instrumental variables; regression discontinuity design; propensity score matching and regression; difference in difference.

EC438.title: Experimental Economics
EC438.description: A brief history of controlled experiments in economics; methodology of experimental design and hypothesis testing; review and discussion of results from experiments on individual decision making, simultaneous and sequential games, social preferences, trust, reciprocity, public goods and coordination problems. Programming computer-based experiments.

EC439.title: Behavioral Economics
EC439.description: Introduction to classical models of decision making; bounded rationality and behavioral biases; behavioral models of choice under uncertainty, intertemporal choice, overconfidence, fairness, reasoning in multi-player games. Using behavioral economics for public policy.

EC442.title: Game Theoretical Models of Political Economy
EC442.description: Models of voter participation—pivotal voter model, ethical voter model, uncertain voter model; strategic voting; electoral competition—Downsian electoral competition, median-voter equilibria, probabilistic voting; electoral systems; theory of political regimes and transitions.

EC447.title: The Political Economy of the Environment
EC447.description: Analysis of environmental and natural resource allocations among competing individuals, groups, and classes; interplay between values and institutions in environmental problem-solving; common pool resources; financialisation of nature and environmental ethics; ecological distribution conflicts; challenges of global environmental governance. Case studies on issues such as fisheries, forest management, biodiversity conservation, climate change.

EC449.title: Topics in Banking and Finance
EC449.description: Functions of banks; asymmetric information in financial markets; bank management, risk management; competition in banking; banking and financial crises; banking regulation, Basel capital accord; lender of last resort; issues in credit and deposit markets.

EC454.title: Turkish Tax System
EC454.description: Historical development of the Turkish tax system. Structure of the tax system, taxes based on income, taxes based on expenditures, taxes based on wealth and transfer of wealth, elasticity of the tax system and tax burden.

EC465.title: Computational Methods in Macroeconomics
EC465.description: Selected data sources; introduction to statistical and econometric programming (EViews and STATA); introduction to computation and solution methods (MATLAB); numerical economic modeling and computational applications of life-cycle permanent income hypothesis; real business cycle theory and other general equilibrium models; numerical dynamic programming.

EC470.title: Turkish Economy
EC470.description: The evolution of the structure and institutions of Turkish economy; growth, production, trade and distribution patterns; evolution of economic policy and current economic issues.

EC471.title: Growth and Development
EC471.description: Concepts and measurement of growth and development; a survey of conventional, non-conventional and critical theories of growth and development; the identification of major problems of economic development and globalisation.

EC474.title: Topics in International Development
EC474.description: The evolution of the post war international economic order; development strategies and country experiences in a comparative perspective; a survey of leading issues in economic development.

EC475.title: European Union - Turkey Economic Relations
EC475.description: Economic policies of the European Union (trade policy, competition policy, industrial policy, the Common Agricultural Policy, regional policy) and their implications for Turkey; trade and investment relations with the European Union; capital and labor mobility; the impact of the Customs Union. Other economic policy issues.
EC475.prerequisite: EC 205 or POLS 343 or POLS 344. EC 480-489 Special Topics in Economics (3+2+0) 3 ECTS 6 (Ekonomide Özel Konular)

EC490.title: Directed Reading and Research
EC490.description:
Members of the Economics Department give reading and research assignments to students and supervise the progress of these projects. The circumstances where such projects are warranted are to be determined by the faculty members. The scope and duration of the reading and research projects are to be indicated at the beginning of the semester.

AD101.title: Introduction to Management
AD101.description: An introductory survey of the business world, government and society; basic business functions and their interrelationships; production, finance, marketing, research and development; introduction to management functions; organization.

AD204.title: Business Communications
AD204.description: Development of oral and written communication skills; memoranda and report writing; communicating in international contexts; public speech; and presentations.

AD211.title: Financial Accounting for Economists
AD211.description: Introduction to basic concepts and principles of accounting, accounting and book-keeping; the balance sheet equation, effects of transactions on the accounting equation, double-entry bookkeping, concept of debit and credit, the general journal and posting of transactions, preparing a trial balance, adjusting the accounts and preparing the income statement and balance sheet, merchandising concern, detailed analysis of basic accounts: cash, accounts receivable and notes receivable, inventories and inventory valuation methods.

AD213.title: Financial Accounting
AD213.description: Introduction to basic concepts and principles of accounting based on International Financial Reporting Standards. Recording business transactions and year-end adjustments, preparation of trial balance, balance sheet and income statement; opening and closing the accounts; analysis of major accounts. The use and interpretation of financial reports. The concepts and standards for the measurements used in preparing the financial statements of businesses.

AD214.title: Managerial Accounting
AD214.description:
Introduction to the use of accounting information by managers to plan and control business transactions of a firm with emphasis on

planning information systems and managerial control systems. Using accounting information for decision making; techniques for estimating fixed and variable costs. Budgeting process; operating budgets; bridging planning and control; cash budgeting; budgetary control and variance analysis; cost allocations; transfer pricing.

AD216.title: IE Financial and Cost Accounting
AD216.description: An introduction to accounting concepts, principles, standards, and their application to transaction analysis. Preparation and interpretation of financial statements; determination and reporting of net income and financial position. Discussion of managerial accounting topics such as the planning and controlling of firm operations. An introduction to cost behavior, budgeting, responsibility accounting, cost control, and product costing.

AD220.title: Management of Organizations
AD220.description: An introductory course in management theory and practice; management as a discipline and as a process. Evolution and scope of management, decision making, planning, organizing, leading and controlling.

AD242.title: Strategic Marketing Management
AD242.description: Introduction to the fundamental principles, concepts and analytical techniques related to the role of marketing in the profit and not- for-profit organizations and in the economy. Strategic planning, and strategic marketing, elements of the marketing mix, consumer behavior, competitive strategies, evaluation of marketing management. Group exercises and field study on new product development, pricing, distribution, integrated marketing communications and positioning.

AD251.title: Managerial Statistics I
AD251.description:
Presentation and interpretation of data; basic probability theory; theoretical distributions; problems of estimation and tests of hypotheses.

AD 252 Managerial Statistics II ( 3+2+0) 3 ECTS 5

(Yönetim İstatistiği II )

Simple regression and correlation; multiple regression and correlation; selected topics in regression analysis; index numbers; time-series analysis.

AD302.title: Business Analytics
AD302.description: Core skills with programming tools for data science; data wrangling, exploration, and visualization. Supervised and unsupervised machine learning models for data-oriented examples within business context.

AD311.title: Financial Management
AD311.description: The time value of money; discounted cash flow analysis; valuing financial assets. Capital budgeting; risk and return; cost of capital; corporate financing decisions; and introduction to capital structure.

AD312.title: Money and Banking
AD312.description: The course is designed to provide the student with basic concepts such as financial liberalization, demand and supply of money and other financial assets, creation of money by the central bank, the banking system and by other financial intermediaries, the money base, money multiplier, velocity of money and the monetary policy. Furthermore the Turkish legal and institutional structure is highlighted and compared to the financial structure of the EC economies. Money and capital markets, the foreign exchange market, interbank markets and government security auctions as well as open market operations are discussed, and forward, future and options markets are introduced.

AD314.title: Intermediate Financial Accounting
AD314.description: Focus on asset, liability and owners' equity measurement and timing of recognition issues, together with the associated income determination problems; review of basic accounting concepts, principles and standards; systematic treatment of major items in the financial statements.

AD316.title: Cost Accounting
AD316.description: Managerial cost accumulation systems; job-order costing, process costing; joint product and by product costing; standard costing. Establishment of standards, computation and analysis of variances, journal entries and disposition of variances; direct and absorption costing, relevant costs and revenue in decision making. Inventory costing, customer costing, business process improvement, strategic cost management, the balanced scorecard.

AD351.title: Operations Management
AD351.description: Operations involved in creating products or services, operations strategy and competitiveness, project management, product design and process selection, facility location and layout, supply chain management, just-in time and lean manufacturing systems, enterprise resource planning systems, capacity planning, sales and operations planning, material requirements planning, inventory management, operations scheduling, waiting line management and quality management.

AD352.title: Information Systems Management
AD352.description: Information systems and technologies (IS/IT) in businesses. The role and value of IS/IT in enabling organizational strategies. Application to real-world business problems, use of relational database management sytems, and business data analysis for developing insights. Current issues in IS/IT areas.

AD353.title: Management Science
AD353.description: Decision making versus forecasting and budgeting in management. Taxonomy of mathematical models and modeling processes. Assumptions, cannonical form, geometrical interpretation, reviews of major algorithms, and sensitivity analysis of optimization techniques under certainty. Decision making under uncertainty and game theory. Stochastic programming. Simulation, numerical search algorithms, and heuristics.Prerequisite: MATH 101, MATH 102, AD 251 or consent of the instructor.

AD401.title: Globalization and International Management
AD401.description: Nature of the international system utilizing the concepts of interdependence, reciprocity, cooperation and conflict management. Main agents and problems surrounding their interrelations. Institutions that aim to manage global/regional processes of trade, development financing and investment.
AD401.prerequisite: Senior standing or consent of the instructor.

AD403.title: Managerial Economics
AD403.description: Fundamentals of economic reasoning in decision making contexts. Demand, production, cost theory assumed. Benchmark models of monopoly and oligopoly; quantity and price setting competition, leadership, collusion, product differentiation. Monopoly price discrimination, quantitiy discounts, freight absorption, metering. Transfer pricing. Two-period competitive strategies. Decision theory. Expected utility. Role of risk aversion in insurance, forward transactions, mutual funds. Value of information. Principal-agent problem. Moral hazard and adverse selection.
AD403.prerequisite: Senior standing or consent of the instructor.

AD407.title: Decision Processes
AD407.description: The history and nature of decision-making, decision and uncertain events; decision-making under certainty; cost-volume-profit analysis; prediction (forecasting); a numerical measure for uncertainty; probability concepts, revision and applications, Bayesian approach; values criteria for decision-making under uncertainty; expected value of perfect information; utility as a decision criteria; preference theory. Utility of money; expected value of imperfect information; decision trees; EVSI and economics of sampling; linear programming and constraints as a decision-making tool, special purpose algorithms; assignment scheduling, transportation models, sensitivity analysis; game theory; Markov chains; network analysis; quantitative divisions; past, present and future.

AD408.title: Strategic Management
AD408.description: Strategic management of businesses in different segments of industry, major policy decisions for integrated organizations.
AD408.prerequisite: Senior standing or consent of the instructor.

AD409.title: Business Ethics
AD409.description: An interdisciplinary approach to the analysis of ethical problems and issues arising from management and administrative practices in the private and public sector. Among the topics/issues covered will be relationship of ethics and philosophy, sociology, economics, law and management; code of ethics for students of management, economics and political sciences; honesty and social responsibility in management, health and safety in the workplace, discrimination and employment, ethical leadership, impact of marketing operations, misleading and deceiving advertising, product information and promotion, consumer protection, disadvantaged consumers ecological conscientiousness.

AD410.title: Advance Managerial Accounting
AD410.description: Decision making implications of information provided by accounting theory. Contemporary problems in reporting of financial statements. Presentation format of financial statements as required by the ministry of Finance in Turkey, analysis and interpretation of items appearing on the financial statements; methods of financial statement analysis.

AD411.title: Finance for Creative Industries
AD411.description: Financial decision-making and economics in creative industries, including film, television, music and sports. Business models, characteristics of financial analysis, deal structures and valuation within the highly dynamic and unvertain environment of the industry. The role of finance in the life cycle of a creative idea, from inception to completion and release. Strategic financial decisions at the corporate level. The future of technology and entertainment economics.

AD412.title: Taxation and Accounting
AD412.description: Tax concepts; taxation of business, entities, tax planning, tax rules and regulations; a review of Turkish Income; Corporate and Tax Procedure Laws; Social Security, withholding taxes, value added taxes. Bilingual (English and Turkish).

AD413.title: Auditing
AD413.description: Introduction to conceptual and applied material in the field of auditing; emphasis on the audit process, reporting, and professional responsibilites; auditing standards; financial control techniques.

AD414.title: Advance Financial Management
AD414.description: Valuation of stocks and bonds, capital structure theory, common stock financing, options, warrants and other hybrid securities along with leasing and corporate restructuring namely mergers, acquisitions and divestitures.

AD415.title: Corporate Finance
AD415.description: Analysis of corporate finance topics including dividend policy, capital structure, leasing, real option valuation, risk management, mergers, and acquisitions.

AD416.title: Profit Planning and Control
AD416.description: Principles of planning and control; preparation of budgets and performance reports through use of computer applications.

AD417.title: Strategic Financial Management
AD417.description: Provides a framework for integrating and relating financial decisions to broader corporate policy by elaborating on the effects of different policies on company performance. Determinants of capital structure, agency costs, strategy and effects on capital structure will be some issues that will be covered.

AD418.title: International Finance
AD418.description: The international monetary system, exchange rate determination, foreign exchange markets, international banking, currency futures and options will be the main focus of the course.

AD419.title: International Financial Management
AD419.description: This course is a continuation of AD 418 and emphasizes financial management in an international environment with special reference to topics such as foreign exchange risk, transfer pricing, country risk analysis and exchange rate forecasting.

AD420.title: Entrepreneurial Finance : Financial policies for new ventures
AD420.description: Application of tools and techniques of corporate finance to the entrepreneurial venture. Exposition of differences between entrepreneurial finance and corporate finance.Introduction to theories and financial tools needed by an entrepreneur in starting, building and harvesting a successful business venture. Options in venture financing, valuation, role of risk diversification on investment value. The importance of options as determinants of value. Emphasis on the maximization of value for the entrepreneur in contrast to maximization of value for investors. Focus on indicators of financial distress: ways to rescue a struggling venture. Finance theory and applications in the practice of new ventures.

AD421.title: Public Management
AD421.description: Concepts of discipline; essentials of management of public business; introduction to organizational theory, personnel finance, administration. Functions of the executive; the nature of authority and leadership; communication; problems of public organization and procedures in Turkey.

AD422.title: Psychology in Management
AD422.description: This course aims to focus on the "individual" working in all types of organizations. It applies the theories that are developed in the field of psychology to organizations. In addition to providing theoretical knowledge, secondly, the course focuses on the development skills in leadership and working as a group. Third, the course attempts to facilitate the acquisition of attitudes that will promote positive relationships with others in organizations. In order to achieve these objectives, in addition to lectures, the course includes a wide variety of laboratory practices.

AD424.title: Human Behaviour in Organization
AD424.description: Human behavior in organizations; key interpersonal skills in the field of management. Intra-personal and interpersonal processes, leadership, influencing and persuasion, and motivation in the workplace. Influence of culture on human processes.

AD425.title: Management of Technology
AD425.description: The nature of technologies and the relationship between technology and management techniques, manufacturing versus service technology, technological interdependence and design parameters, departmental technology and its relationship with departmental structure and management. The effective ways of getting things done in different technologies.
AD425.prerequisite: 4th year standing or consent of the instructor.

AD427.title: Human Resources Management
AD427.description: Human resources management and its role in organizational success. Strategic human resources management. Major human resources activities including human resources planning, staffing, training and development, career management, performance management, compensation and employee relations. Tools and best practices in human resources management.
AD427.prerequisite: AD 220 or consent of the instructor.

AD428.title: NGO Management
AD428.description: A historical overview of the private nonprofit sector; economic and political theories of nonprofit organization; the tax treatment of NGO's; scope and theory of government/NGO relations; nonprofit organizations and the market; executive leadership in the NGO's; organizational change in the NGO's; enterprise and commerce in nonprofit organziations; comparative perpectives.

AD429.title: Management of Multinationals
AD429.description: Structural characteristics of Multinational Companies and their relative competitive position in the world market. Multinational business strategies based on product/market evolution. Management techniques required to achieve the macro strategies in macro-environments in which multinationals are imbedded (economic, technological, social/cultural and legal).

AD430.title: Turkish Business Environment
AD430.description: The nature of the business environment: theories and techniques; The Turkish economy, past and present and international competitiveness. Foreign direct investment, state and business relations and business associations in Turkey. Structural analysis of major sectors and the geographic distribution of economic activity in Turkey.

AD432.title: Entrepreneurship
AD432.description:
Entrepreneurship framework and definition; entrepreneurship as a profession. Small businesses and entrepreneurship in Turkey; from creativity to entrepreneurship. Creativity and innovation; recognition and evaluation of the opportunity. Preparing a business plan; funding the venture; raising money as seed and growth capital; venture capital; valuation of ventures. Succession planning; selling a venture; mergers and acquisitions for ventures.

AD 433 Management Simulation (3+0+0) 3 / ECTS 6

(Yönetim Simulasyonu)

Use of technical and academic knowledge in accounting, finance, organization theory and behavior, human resource management, marketing, production and logistics in a simulated business environment. Executive C-level decisions in a simulated corporate environment and the results of these actions in a competitive environment.
AD432.prerequisite: Senior standing or consent of the instructor.

AD439.title: Business-to-Business Marketing
AD439.description: Fundamental concepts and theories underlying the marketing activities between businesses. Business market analysis. Segmentation, targeting and positioning of busienss markets based on needs. Marketing mix elements and competitive strategies. Marketing plans and projects for developing new business products with effective pricing, promotion and distribution strategies.
AD439.prerequisite: AD 242 or consent of the instructor.

AD440.title: Digital Marketing
AD440.description: Focus on the role of digital media in bringing strategic and behavioral changes to companies and consumers. Analysis of new tools and concepts such as social media, search engines, online brand communities, viral, mobile, and content marketing. Discussion of the impact of interactive communication platforms on companies and consumers. Extending the understanding of digital marketing within company strategies, and its application together with traditional marketing tools.
AD440.prerequisite: AD 242 or consent of the instructor.

AD441.title: Consumer Behavior
AD441.description: Introduction to theories, models and findings drawn from, among others, the behavioral sciences on consumer behavior. Review of literature on perception, learning, motivation, attitude formation and change. Behavioral models and their application in marketing and managerial decision making process.
AD441.prerequisite: AD 242 or consent of the instructor.

AD442.title: Advertising
AD442.description: The role of advertising in the marketing mix and its economic and social effects; advertising agencies, advertising campaign management - budgeting, media selection, and creation of the advertisement measurement of the effectiveness of advertising.
AD442.prerequisite: AD 242 or consent of the instructor.

AD444.title: Sales Management
AD444.description: Study of concepts and techniques underlying sales management, buyer-seller interaction, nature of the sales job; personal selling in the marketing mix. Measurement of market and sales potentials; sales forecasting techniques; sales territories.
AD444.prerequisite: AD 242 or consent of the instructor.

AD445.title: Retail Management
AD445.description: Competitive developments in retail management; store location, building and interior layout; merchandise management; buying, handling, control and pricing; sales promotion and customer service; personnel management; coordination and control in retail management.
AD445.prerequisite: AD 242 or consent of the instructor.

AD446.title: Marketing Research
AD446.description: Basic research issues in formulating strategies for product, pricing, promotion and distribution decisions; development of measurement scales for descriptive and experimental designs; introduction to statistical package computer programs; probability sampling, univariate and multivariate data analysis methods.
AD446.prerequisite: AD 302, AD 252, AD 242 or consent of the instructor.

AD447.title: Services Marketing
AD447.description: Assessing the processes in the services marketing situations and to develop related perspectives. Critical strategic factors regarding pre-purchase, purchase, and post-purchase of services; contextual, situational and interpersonal determinants in service encounters and post-purchase dis/satisfaction.
AD447.prerequisite: AD 242 or consent of the instructor.

AD448.title: Brand Management
AD448.description: Presentation of foundations for developing marketing plans by providing an understanding of the conceptual realm of brand strategy, developing and measuring brand equity.
AD448.prerequisite: AD 242 or consent of the instructor.

AD451.title: Management of Constraints
AD451.description: Establishing the goal of the company and identifying the measurements that determine the effect of each action on company profit. Focusing on both physical constraints such as capacity, market, as well as policy constraints such as the decisions or rules that make up the mode of operation. Achieving a process of ongoing improvement by implementing simple, logical, and clearly defined processes that satisfy a significant need of clients much better than competition; needs such as reliability, rapid response, increasing inventory turnovers and sales by ensuring the availability of products, maximizing income per shelf, and finishing projects on time and within budget without sacrificing the content.
AD451.prerequisite: AD 351 or consent of the instructor.

AD453.title: Quality Management
AD453.description: Principles of quality management and control systems. Design and development of quality systems in manufacturing and service sectors. Quality improvement programs. Quality information systems.

AD454.title: Predictive Analytics
AD454.description: Introduction to analytical methods used to extract insights from data through case studies and representative datasets. General principles of classification and prediction algorithms. Understanding data science concepts behind a wide set of data mining techniques and their relation to managerial decision problems.

AD455.title: Data Analytics for Business
AD455.description: Learning how to manage real-world data analytics projects using data gathered from organizations. Exploring all aspects of the data science process from business understanding to problem definition; from data ingestion and data transformation to modeling, model evaluation, reporting, and visualization.

AD458.title: Forecasting
AD458.description: Forecasting in management fields; demand forecasting; data aggregation and pyramid forecasting. Statistical versus operational measures of forecast accuracy; overview of judgemental, statistical and hybrid forecasting methods. Time series forecasting methods and leading professional software packages. Design of simulation tests for proper selection of a forecasting method; combining competing forecasts.

AD459.title: Supply Chain Management
AD459.description: A comprehensive coverage of topics in the design and management of the supply chain; supply chain modeling, inventory management, risk pooling, value of information, supply chain partnerships, international issues, and decision support systems.
AD459.prerequisite: AD 351, AD 353. AD 460 E-Commerce (3+0+0) 3 / ECTS 6 (E-Ticaret) E-commerce business models, planning, start-ups and entrepreneurship. E-commerce technical infrastructure and payment systems. Logistics and fulfillment for e-commerce. Legal regulations surrounding e-commerce. Website user interface design and user experience. Internet advertising and marketing including the role of social media and search engine marketing and optimization. Customer analytics and customer relationship management for e-commerce. Senior standing or consent of the instructor.

AD462.title: Legal Aspects of Intellectual Property Management
AD462.description: Notions of patents, trademarks, copyright and related rights. Protection of industrial designs, geographical indications, know-how, trade secrets and confidential information. Management of intellectual property rights in the e-commerce and biotechnology industries. The organizational, administrative and legal framework of intellectual property law; national and international legislation. Innovation and knowledge transfer; university and industry collaborations; technology transfer and licensing agreements; commercialisation of R&D output and intellectual assets.

AD463.title: Labor-Management Relations
AD463.description: The practice of collective bargaining in the development and maintenance of good labor relations. Labor policies and operating procedures affecting the relationships between the parties. Their mutual rights and obligations. Contact negotiation techniques in conciliation and arbitration procedures to break deadlock.

AD465.title: Fixed Income Securities
AD465.description: An introduction to bonds and other debt instruments. Covers the models and techniques required to price and analyze fixed income securities and their derivatives. Includes the basic concepts of fixed income instruments, such as yield, duration, convexity; pricing traditional derivatives such as swaps and bond options; management of fixed income portfolios and hedging of associated risks. An elementary introduction to term structure of interest rates and credit risk modeling, and their use in valuation of derivative instruments.
AD465.prerequisite: AD 311 or consent of the instructor

AD466.title: Introduction to Financial Derivatives
AD466.description: An introduction to pricing, trading and hedging of financial derivatives such as futures, options, and swaps. Topics include stochastic modeling of the financial markets; concept of arbitrage; valuation of financial derivatives; Black-Scholes model; trading strategies; hedging techniques; volatility smile and exotic options. Applications of basic numerical procedures such as binomial trees and Monte Carlo simulation.
AD466.prerequisite: AD 311 or consent of the instructor

AD467.title: Corporate Governance
AD467.description: The concepts of corporate ownership and governance. Compliance with securities laws and regulation, codes of best practice, role of the board of directors, impact of external competition, long-term economic value of the corporation, current issues and challenges in corporate governance.

AD468.title: Financial Risk Management
AD468.description: Introduction to the principles and practises of financial risk management for businesses. Recognizing and understanding the different types of risks faced by businesses. Controlling risk; quantifying financial risk; features of risk measurement tools; metrics used to manage financial risks.
AD468.prerequisite: AD 311 or consent of the instructor.

AD469.title: Valuation
AD469.description: Examination of major approaches to valuation of securities: Discounted cash flow models; relative valuation through multiples; valuation through real options. Analysis of the basics of risk; market efficiency; riskfree rates and risk premiums; measuring earnings; estimating cash flows and growth; interpreting financial multiples. Application of the above mentioned tools to valuation of publicly traded firms, private firms and financial institutions.
AD469.prerequisite: AD 311 or consent of the instructor.

AD470.title: Investment Management
AD470.description: Introduction to the process of investing in financial securities. Overviews of the investment decision-making process and, of securities markets and trading practices. Asset pricing models; principles of modern portfolio theory; performance measurement techniques; asset allocation strategies; fixed income securities. Introduction to derivative securities, risk management strategies.

AD471.title: Accounting Systems Design
AD471.description: Designing an accounting system; understanding the flow of information to and from accounting deparment; collection, processing and communication of accounting information; application of computers in accounting. Students will be assigned a term project.

AD472.title: Financial Markets and Institutions
AD472.description: Structure of financial markets and financial institutions. Overview of interest rates and security valuation. Central banking system and monetary policy; securities markets including money, capital, foreign exchange, and derivatives markets. Commercial banks; investment banks; insurance companies; mutual funds. Introduction to financial risk management.
AD472.prerequisite: AD 311 or consent of the instructor.

AD473.title: International Accounting
AD473.description: Similarities and differences of accounting principles and procedures between Turkey and other countries, mainly members of European Community and Turkic countries; regional and worldwide standardization, consolidation of foreign subsidaries, performance evaluation of foreign operations, statement analysis; emphasis on accounting in multinational enterprises.

AD474.title: Invesment and Financial Data Analysis
AD474.description: The study of financial investment theory; financial statistical modelling and financial empirical analyses. Asset pricing and risk management using multivariate probability distributions; estimation, testing and forecasts; time series data; cross-sectional data.
AD474.prerequisite: AD 311 or consent of the instructor.

AD475.title: Advanced Financial Accounting
AD475.description: Emphasis on topics like consolidated financial statements; inflation accounting; leasing accounting, disclosure of financial statements; segments reporting; interm reporting and other special topics.
AD475.prerequisite: AD 311 or consent of the instructor.

AD476.title: Financial Simulation
AD476.description: Financial market relations of public and private institutions analyzed in a simulated computerized environment.

AD477.title: Bank Management
AD477.description: The major issues behind effective bank management.

AD478.title: Insurance Management
AD478.description: The Turkish Insurance Market and important aspects in insurance are reviewed. The types of insurance and insurers are analyzed. The balance sheet and the income statement of a typical insurance company, pricing of insurance products, financial analysis, management of underwriting and financial portfolios, planning, marketing, organization, information systems in an insurance company are the topics covered in the course.
AD478.prerequisite: AD 311. AD 479 Accounting for Non-Profit Organizations (3+0+0) 3 (Kar Amacı Gütmeyen Kuruluşlarda Muhasebe) Emphasis on accounting, budgeting, auditing and reporting policies and practices for government, state-economic enterpreses, municipalities and other non-profit organiziations including universites, hospitals, charities. AD 211 or AD 214 or AD 216.

AD480.title: Special Topics in Management
AD480.description: This course aims to study topics related to current issues and trends in management theory and practices. The course is to be run in a workshop format with active student participation.
AD480.prerequisite: AD 220 or consent of the instructor.

AD481.title: Special Topics in Operations Management
AD481.description: Current issues and topics of interest in operations management.

AD482.title: Special Topics in Information Systems
AD482.description: Current issues and topics of interest in information management.
AD482.prerequisite: AD 352 or consent of the instructor.

AD484.title: Special Topics in Marketing
AD484.description: In depth analysis of marketing topics and cases of current interest.
AD484.prerequisite: AD 242 or consent of the instructor.

AD488.title: Special Topics in Accounting
AD488.description: In depth analysis of topics and cases of current interest.

AD489.title: Current Issues in Accounting
AD489.description: Current issues and topics of interest in accounting.
AD489.prerequisite: AD 211 or AD 214 or AD 216 or consent of the instructor. AD 490 Topics in Game Theory and Managerial Economics (3+0+0) 3 (Oyun Teorisi ve Yönetim Ekonomisi) Representative topics are incomplete information games, markets with asymmetric information, cooperative games, mechanism design, joint ownership and distribution, matching markets, auctions, principal-agent problems. AD 403.

AD491.title: Advanced Topics in Operations Research
AD491.description: Advanced topics in linear programming, revised simplex, integer programming, goal programming, heuristic programming, dynamic programming.

AD492.title: Special Topics in Management Science
AD492.description: Topics of interest in Management Science to be selected to suit both the class and the faculty.

AD495.title: Special Topics in Corporate Finance
AD495.description: Current issues and topics in corporate finance.
AD495.prerequisite: AD 311 or consent of the instructor.

AD496.title: Special Topics in Finance
AD496.description: Current issues and topics of interest in finance.
AD496.prerequisite: AD 311 or consent of the instructor.

AD497.title: Bachelor of Arts Degree Project
AD497.description: Integration of management topics, marketing, finance and accounting, and operations, in a project developing a business plan by forecasting economic, social, political, and technological trends in business and social environment.
AD497.prerequisite: Senior standing or consent of the instructor.
