POLS101.title: Introduction to Political Science
POLS101.description: Introduction to the study of politics. Terminology and methodology of political science. Government and administration. Executive, legislative, and judiciary. Governance, political participation, political actors, government structures and processes. Basic concepts of political theory, comparative politics and international relations.

POLS201.title: History of Political Thought I
POLS201.description: Study of ancient Greek, Roman, and medieval political thinkers. Analysis of their major contributions to the development of political theory.

POLS202.title: History of Political Thought II
POLS202.description: Analysis of the works of the major Western political theorists from Machiavelli to the present, with emphasis on general developments, trends, and basic issues in modern political theory.

POLS203.title: Social Statistics
POLS203.description: Introduction to statistical methods in social sciences. Basic descriptive and inferential techniques.

POLS206.title: Political Science Research Methods
POLS206.description: Introduction to theory-oriented research in political science: Research problems, research designs, quantitative data collection techniques, data processing, data analysis, and interpretation of social science data with special emphasis on quantitative methods used in data analysis, and report writing on the basis of data analysis and findings.

POLS215.title: Comparative Politics
POLS215.description: Major concepts and theoretical approaches in comparative politics. Comparative party systems, electoral systems, political institutions, state-society relations, democratization, and political culture.

POLS217.title: Diplomatic History
POLS217.description: History of diplomacy and international relations from the French Revolution to the end of the Cold War. The emergence of balance of power systems, nationalism, colonialism, the World Wars, decolonization and the Cold War.

POLS242.title: Introduction to International Relations
POLS242.description: The rise and evolution of the nation-state system, the operation of balance of power, deterrence, coercion, conflict, diplomacy, crisis management, and the role of international law and institutions in inter-state relations.

POLS246.title: Introduction to Turkish Politics
POLS246.description: The development of the Turkish political system from the Ottoman period to the present with emphasis on the interaction of state, politics, and society.
POLS246.prerequisite: POLS 101 or Consent of the Instructor.

POLS303.title: Fundamentals of Political Economy
POLS303.description: An introduction to the basic concepts, theories and methodologies of political economy. The interaction between states and markets and between power and wealth at domestic and international contexts.

POLS340.title: Foreign Policy
POLS340.description: Foreign policy making processes and analyses. Politics and foreign policy. Actors, interests and interactions. Turkey's international relations and foreign policy making as a case study.

POLS472.title: Comparative Political Systems
POLS472.description: Comparison of political systems of North America and Western Europe. Emphasis on Great Britain, France, and the Federal Republic of Germany. Historical legacies, key political institutions, and political culture.
POLS472.prerequisite: POLS 101. ELECTIVE COURSES BY SUBFIELDS (OFFERED PERIODICALLY) COMPARATIVE POLITICS

POLS304.title: Development of Contemporary Democracies
POLS304.description: Examination of the historical origins and development of democracy in a comparative perspective, with emphasis on major historical processes and contemporary debates.

POLS305.title: Politics of Nationalism and Ethnicity
POLS305.description: Nationalism and nation-building in historical perspective. Ethnicity, national consciousness, and ethnic nationalism in an international and comparative framework.

POLS307.title: Secularism and its Critiques
POLS307.description:
The etymological, philosophical, scientific and historical origins of secularism. A survey of the contemporary political philosophical critiques of secularism. An evaluation of the relation between secularism and democracy.

Prerequisite¨POLS 101.

POLS308.title: Politics in Developing Countries
POLS308.description: The structures and processes of politics in developing countries with special attention on the dynamics of regime changes.

POLS310.title: Comparative Electoral System
POLS310.description: Properties of various electoral systems in comparative perspective. Theory and practice of elections. Plurality systems, proportional systems.

POLS311.title: Politics of Latin America
POLS311.description: The structures and political processes in Latin American countries with a focus on populism, revolution, authoritarianism, and democracy. Historical and theoretical examination of political change and economic development in the region.

POLS314.title: Politics and Cinema
POLS314.description: Politics as seen through the lens of selected movie directors. Critical appraisal of classical and contemporary political films and of the main political issues projected to the screen. Exploration of the political and social relevance of cinema.

POLS317.title: Politics and Society in the Middle East
POLS317.description: A general introduction to histories, peoples and politics of the Middle East. Colonialism, imperialism, orientalism, state, institutions, popular culture, nationalism, democratization, political Islam, patriarchy, social movements.

POLS320.title: Politics in Asia and the Pacific
POLS320.description: Comparative analysis of political change and rapid economic development in East and Southeast Asia, with particular focus on Japan, China, and the East Asian NICs.

POLS323.title: Politics of Identity
POLS323.description: Theoretical perspectives on the politicization of gender, religion, ethnicity and locality. The construction of political identities in modern and postmodern socio-political culture, particularly in relation to key political concepts such as public sphere, state, law, nationality, citizenship and community.

POLS330.title: Political Geography
POLS330.description: Relationship between politics and territory. State boundaries, demographics, socioeconomic characteristics and activities.

POLS332.title: Political Sociology
POLS332.description: Development of the modern state, the relationship of the state to society, with special emphasis on the nature of modern political institutions and processes.
POLS332.prerequisite: POLS 101, SOC 101, SOC 108. POLS 333 Local Politics and Democracy (3+0+0) 3 / ECTS 5 (Yerel Siyaset ve Demokrasi) Examination of local politics, government and governance with specific focus on citizen participation and democracy in comparative perspective. POLS 101

POLS347.title: Administrative Law
POLS347.description: Introduction to the organization, powers and operation of the administrative structure of government. Judicial review.

POLS361.title: Politics and Law
POLS361.description: An interdisciplinary approach to the relationship between the constitution and the political system, political processes and judicial review of legislative acts. Case studies from the Turkish, Continental European, and Anglo-American contexts.

POLS404.title: Religion and Society
POLS404.description: Political, sociological, anthropological and economic approaches to the status of religions in today's world. Secularism in the East and in the West. Comparative analysis of political, social, cultural, scientific, economic and gender issues involved in secularization and desecularization.

POLS405.title: Communications and Politics
POLS405.description: The global revolution in mass communication and its impact on political processes, cultural identity, national and global issues.

POLS410.title: Political Behavior
POLS410.description: Impact of psychological, cultural and social structural factors on individual and mass behavior in political life, with emphasis on voting behavior.

POLS413.title: Political Parties and Party Systems
POLS413.description: Comparative analysis of the origins, functions and organizational characteristics of political parties and interest groups in different political systems.

POLS415.title: Political Psychology
POLS415.description: Introduction to the theories and empirical findings on political cognition, attitudes, values and beliefs. Theories of political socialization, political action, and protest behavior.

POLS416.title: Literature and Politics
POLS416.description: Study of works of literature as sources for understanding.

POLS417.title: From Weimar to Berlin
POLS417.description: Analysis of social and political problems leading to the collapse of the Weimar Republic, rise and fall of the Third Reich, the establishment of the Federal Republic, and German Unification.

POLS421.title: Comparative State and Bureaucracy
POLS421.description: Typologies of states and bureaucracies with particular emphasis on the relationship in different political systems.

POLS424.title: Social Movements
POLS424.description: Introduction to the theory of social movements. Case studies of old and new types of social movements in a comparative perspective. Worker, woman and immigrant movements.

POLS432.title: Political Economy of Exclusion
POLS432.description: Exploring various dimensions and modalities of human deprivation and exclusion. Study of linkages between globalization and exclusion, various theories on marginality, poverty, informality and inequality, analysis of political solutions and strategies.

POLS445.title: Current Issues in European Integration
POLS445.description: Problems and prospects of European economic and political integration. EU enlargement. Post-Maastricht developments and current debates.

POLS452.title: Migrants, Refugees and Politics: Comparative Perspectives
POLS452.description: Analysis of the past and present of transnational migratory movements; selected case studies including Turkey and the EU; comparison of different migration and asylum policies and their social and political impact on destination countiries.

POLS466.title: Human Rights: Theory and Practice
POLS466.description: Theoretical foundations and historical development of human rights. Evolution of international human rights regimes and their impact on international and domestic politics.

POLS473.title: Theories and Politics of Authoritarian and Totalitarian Regimes
POLS473.description: Examination of authoritarianisms and totalitarianisms of the 20th and 21st centuries as regime types, systems of law, economic systems and political movements, with specific focus on the Frankfurt School’s writings on the Nazi Germany.

POLS474.title: Islam and Politics
POLS474.description: Analysis of the relationship of Islam to politics. Islamist movements in theoretical and comparative perspective.

POLS475.title: Justice as Equality
POLS475.description: A political philosophy-based survey on the answers provided by some of the most prominent political philosophers to the question “if justice is equality, then it is the equality of what?” with specific focus on the implications of having equal liberties.

POLS476.title: Gender and Politics in the Middle East
POLS476.description: Theoretical exploration of gender and politics in the Middle East. Analysis of feminist criticism of basic concepts of politics related to the dynamics of politics in the region.

POLS482.title: Selected Topics in Comparative Politics
POLS482.description: Advanced Seminar on selected topics in comparative politics.

POLS321.title: Theories of International Relations
POLS321.description: Contending theories of international relations. Realism, neorealism, theories of integration and interdependence, constructivism, postmodernist and feminist approaches. Paradigmatic changes and major debates.

POLS324.title: International Law
POLS324.description: Nature and function of international law. Analysis of trends in its development. Principles of public and private international law.

POLS326.title: Twentieth Century Diplomatic History
POLS326.description: In depth coverage of twentieth century diplomatic history. Causes and consequences of the two world wars, the emergence of the bipolar system, post-Cold War developments and conflicts.

POLS327.title: History of International Economic Relations
POLS327.description: International economic relations since World War II, globalization of finance, trade and production.

POLS329.title: Environment and Politics
POLS329.description: Political development and dynamics of environmental issues, with reference to both domestic and international contexts. Green movement and its implications for post-industrial politics. Environmental consequences of current political attitudes.

POLS345.title: Middle East In World Politics
POLS345.description: Historical evolution of the modern Middle East since the decline of the Ottoman Empire. Fundamental issues of the Middle East in contemporary world politics.

POLS346.title: International Organizations
POLS346.description: Typology of international organizations, nature of decision making processes in IGOs. The role and impact of international organizations in world politics.

POLS420.title: International Political Economy
POLS420.description: The interdependence of economic and political factors at the international level with special emphasis on the politicization of international economic relations.

POLS425.title: Politics of Caucasus and Central Asia
POLS425.description: Political dynamics and developments in the Caucasus and Central Asia in the Post-Cold War period.

POLS426.title: Balkan Politics
POLS426.description: Social and political dynamics of Balkan states with emphasis on the causes and consequences of instability in the region.

POLS438.title: Diplomatic Negotiations
POLS438.description: Methods and strategies of conducting diplomatic negotiations.

POLS439.title: Diplomacy and Foreign Policy Analysis
POLS439.description: Survey of the theoretical literature on the study of diplomacy of selected countries.

POLS440.title: Current Issues in World Politics
POLS440.description: Current developments in issues and problem areas of international politics.

POLS443.title: Strategic Studies
POLS443.description: The logic of the post-war bipolar system based on nuclear deterrence, the arms race, disarmament and arms control negotiations.

POLS446.title: European Security
POLS446.description: Comparison of the Cold War and post-Cold War eras. The search for a new security architecture of Europe.

POLS447.title: Soviet Successor States In World Politics
POLS447.description: Changing power configuration in Europe and Asia after the dissolution of the Soviet Union, with emphasis on foreign policy implications.

POLS449.title: International Conflict Analysis
POLS449.description: Review of conflict theories. Understanding the causes of international conflict. Dynamics of conflict escalation, management, settlement, and resolution.
POLS449.prerequisite: POLS 101, POLS 242. POLS 101.

POLS454.title: The Black Sea In World Politics
POLS454.description: Politics of the Black Sea region, with special emphasis on implications for regional and global politics. Political, economic, and security aspects of the region.

POLS455.title: North-South Relations
POLS455.description: Developing countries in global politics in the post-World War II period, with special emphasis on alternative explanations of inequality among nations, and the consequences of the end of the Cold War for the future of North-South relations.

POLS461.title: Peace and Conflict
POLS461.description: Survey of psychological, social, political and religious factors shaping conflict. Analyses of theories of peace, peacebuilding, and reconciliation. Management, transformation and resolution of conflict.

POLS464.title: The Law of International Institutions
POLS464.description: Development and nature of the principles, structures, and legal processes of international institutions, with special emphasis on the United Nations.

POLS477.title: Media and Globalization
POLS477.description: Investigation of media and communication systems' connection to globalization. Survey of key debates on media, globalization and politics, the use of media by global political activism and the role of the state in responding to these processes.

POLS485.title: Selected Topics in International Relations
POLS485.description: Advanced seminar on selected topics in international relations.

POLS306.title: Contemporary Political Ideologies
POLS306.description: Study of liberalism, conservatism, socialism, communism, social democracy, nationalism, from their origins in the 18th century to the present.

POLS319.title: Philosophy of Social Sciences
POLS319.description: Ontological, epistemological, and political-ideological underpinnings of the major approaches to social science. Relation of the social and human sciences to natural science.

POLS336.title: Selected Issues in the History of Political Thought
POLS336.description: Comprehensive analysis of the genesis and historical evolution of selected political concepts and controversies. Selected political thinkers and the in-depth appraisal of their contribution to political thought.

POLS339.title: The State and the Public Sphere
POLS339.description: Theoretical perspectives on the analysis of the state, the public sphere and the conceptualization of the public /private dichotomy.

POLS373.title: Politics and Culture
POLS373.description: Articulation of political power relations in the sphere of culture. Processes of ideological hegemony and political legitimacy. Autonomy of culture from politics and the economy. Cultural dimensions of globalization.

POLS375.title: Gender and Politics
POLS375.description: Study of gender in political discourse. The impact of gender on methodological and substantive issues of politics.

POLS402.title: Ethics and Politics
POLS402.description: Theoretical exploration of the relationship between ethics and politics, discussion of major issues and dilemmas, with particular reference to Plato, Aristotle, Machiavelli, Rousseau, Kant, Hegel, Nietzsche and modern theorists.

POLS403.title: Political Philosophy
POLS403.description: Discussion of the scope and the major themes of political philosophy, such as freedom, equality, truth, justice, the public good, rights and obligations.

POLS406.title: Politics, Ideology and Discourse
POLS406.description: Critical appraisal of modern and postmodern theories of ideology and discourse. Discussion of the contribution of contemporary debates in political thought to the theory and practice of discourse.

POLS407.title: Contemporary Marxist and Post-Marxist Theory
POLS407.description: Theoretical overview of 20th century Marxist thought, particularly in its sociological, phenomenological, structural and postmodern variants. The evolution of Marxist theory from Gramsci, Lukács and the Frankfurt School to contemporary thinkers.

POLS408.title: Democratic Theory
POLS408.description: Contextual survey of the development of democratic theory since Hobbes, with special emphasis on contemporary problems.

POLS430.title: Politics of Modernity and Its Critics
POLS430.description: The central traits of modernity in the 19th and 20th centuries and their relation to politics. Turn-of the-century arts, society and culture and their effects on political values, perceptions and practices. A multi-dimensional appraisal of the critiques of modernity.

POLS431.title: Politics of Postmodernity and Its Critics
POLS431.description: The politics of postmodernity from 1968 to our day. The discourse of postmodernity and its effects on political values, perceptions and political movements. A multi-dimensional appraisal of the critiques of postmodernity.

POLS471.title: Current Debates in Social and Political Theory
POLS471.description: Survey of the basic positions of, and the debate between, Marxism, post-Marxism, post-structuralism, deconstructionism, hermeneutics, critical theory and varieties of post-modernist approaches.

POLS483.title: Selected Topics in Political Theory
POLS483.description: Advanced seminar on selected topics in political theory.

POLS309.title: Political Economy of Contemporary Turkey
POLS309.description: Comprehensive examination of the political economy of contemporary Turkey, with particular emphasis on the changing role of the state in the development process.

POLS318.title: State and Bureaucracy in Turkey
POLS318.description: Examination of state tradition in Turkey. Structure of administration, recruitment and corporate interests of the bureaucracy. Bureaucratic politics, relations of bureaucracy with parliament and government. (Formerly Turkish bureaucratic structure).

POLS334.title: Turkish Constitutional Law
POLS334.description: Examination of the emergence and development of parliamentarism in Turkey. Constitutional developments in the Ottoman Empire and the Turkish Republic.

POLS335.title: Turkish Public Law
POLS335.description: General principles of administrative law. Historical overview of administrative law in Turkey. Constitutional and institutional dynamics of Turkish public administration. Civil servants, public services and judicial review of administrative actions.

POLS338.title: Turkish Foreign Policy
POLS338.description: Turkish foreign policy in historical perspective. Interaction of domestic politics and foreign policy. Role of major actors in the formulation and implementation of Turkish foreign policy.

POLS348.title: Problems and Issues in Turkish Politics
POLS348.description: Discussion of current issues in Turkish political life with special emphasis on secularism, civil-military relations, and problems of democracy.

POLS435.title: Issues In Turkish Foreign Policy
POLS435.description: Major issues in Turkey's foreign relations, regional problems and involvement. Evolution of Turkey's foreign policy goals.

POLS451.title: Ottoman Political and Social Institutions
POLS451.description: Survey of the main features of Ottoman society and its institutions. Pre-Ottoman origins, the classical age, the process of decline, the reform movement and the demise of the empire.

POLS484.title: Selected Topics in Turkish Politics
POLS484.description: Examination of selected issues in Turkish government and political processes.

POLS204.title: Advanced Social Statistics
POLS204.description: Decision theory, testing statistical hypotheses, statistical estimation, parametric and nonparametric statistics, correlation and regression analysis.

POLS350.title: Political Economy of Advanced Industrial Countries
POLS350.description: Analysis of various issues and challenges of industrialization that states, firms and unions face in advanced industrial countries. Exploration of the industrial policies of the United States, Japan and Europe.

POLS351.title: Introduction to Public Choice
POLS351.description: Introduction to the interaction between political and economic factors from the perspective of public choice theory. Application of public choice concepts to public policy issues in both developed and developing countries.

POLS353.title: Globalization and Public Policy
POLS353.description: Discussion of the history and nature of globalization and public policy responses to it with a focus on Europe and the OECD countries. Comparative analysis of economic, social and industrial policy responses to challenges raised by globalization of markets.

POLS370.title: Politics and Decision Theory
POLS370.description: Introduction to the basic concepts of game theory and decision theory as they apply to political science.

POLS422.title: Politics of Markets and Capitalism
POLS422.description: Discussion of major approaches to capitalism and markets by an analysis of ethnographies of economy. Political economy, exchange, production, informality, performativity of modern sciences, market design, commodity circulation, and finance.

POLS423.title: Comparative Political Economy
POLS423.description: Institutionalism as a major strand of political economy. Domestic structures and inter-country variations in public choice and economic performance.

POLS470.title: Formal Modeling in Political Science
POLS470.description: Review of recent applications of game theory and of decision theory in recent formal models of voting and party competition theory and rational choice in international relations and comparative politics.

POLS343.title: Introduction to European Integration
POLS343.description: A study of the evolution of the European integration project from the European Coal and Steel Community to the present European Union, with emphasis on the politics of the deepening of integration and the expansion of EU membership.

POLS344.title: Turkey and the European Union
POLS344.description: History and diplomacy of Turkey's relationship with the European integration process, from the Ankara Treaty to the present. Major issues in EU-Turkey relations.

POLS364.title: Comparative Political Economy of Europe
POLS364.description: Comparative analysis of the major European Union economies including Germany, France, Britain and Italy. Study of the impact of the European integration on these economies.

POLS418.title: European Foreign and Security Policy
POLS418.description: Examination of the evolution toward a common European foreign ad security policy. Policy-making in the EU vis-à-vis major issues in international affairs.

POLS448.title: European Union Institutions and Policy Making
POLS448.description: A basic understanding of the participants, factors and constraints that influence EU policy-making in its various arenas, levels, and stages. Analyzes of the capacity of EU institutions that monitor the enforcement of compliance with EU policy goals, strategies and outcomes in member states.

POLS456.title: Topics in European Integration
POLS456.description: In-depth examination of selected issues and concepts on European integration such as European citizenship and identity, immigration and asylum, local government and regionalism, and institutional reform.

POLS457.title: Issues of Culture and Identity in the European Union
POLS457.description: Current developments in the European Union with regard to culture, identity and citizenship. Issues of immigration, human rights, gender relations, and new social movements.

POLS465.title: European Union Law
POLS465.description: Study of European Union law and legal processes, with emphasis on acquis communautaire and the European Court of Justice. Issues related to jurisdiction and enforcement.

POLS479.title: American Foreign Policy
POLS479.description: Issues and problems in contemporary American foreign policy, focus on different theories and doctrines, with respect to their effect on American foreign policy, analysis of factors determining the US foreign policy.

POLS480.title: Field Research Workshop I
POLS480.description: Field research projects carried out by students from the selection of a research problem to drafting of a final report.

POLS481.title: Field Research Workshop II
POLS481.description: Field research projects carried out by students from the selection of a research problem to drafting of a final report.

POLS486.title: Directed Research and Reading I
POLS486.description: Individual research projects or intensive reading for specialization in field of interest.

POLS487.title: Directed Research and Reading II
POLS487.description: Individual research projects or intensive reading for specialization in field of interest.

POLS497.title: Honors Seminar
POLS497.description:
Students with a minimum GPA of 3.00 will be admitted to this course. Each student will be required to complete a senior thesis under the direction of a faculty member.

AMERICAN STUDIES CERTIFICATE PROGRAM

The American Studies Certificate Program is offered by the School of Arts and Sciences, Department of Western Languages. This program offers an interdisciplinary focus on American culture. Bogazici University students may participate in the program as of their third semester. They are expected to complete the 21 credit program by the time of their graduation, with a cumulative average of 2.50 or above. There are no prerequisites for the two required courses.

The program consists of a required orientation course (AS 250) and five other relevant courses selected from the departments of History, Political Science and International Relations, Sociology and Western Languages and Literatures as well as (AS 412), a research and writing course leading to a thesis to be defended before a jury of three faculty members from different disciplines.

POLS313.description: Analysis of U.S. society and socio-political developments through the works of American authors since mid-19th century, with emphasis on social change as reflected in the novel.

POLS342.title: American Government
POLS342.description: Survey of contemporary US government, with emphasis on the functioning of the federal system, the powers of the presidency, Congress, and the Supreme Court.

TRM101.title: Introduction to Tourism Industry
TRM101.description: Tourism history and introductory principles as: Tourism in perspective; cultural tourism; sociology of tourism; tourism psychology and motivation as to the different features of the total tourism product. Total tourism product such as accommodation units, leisure and recreation facilities; transportation, travel, cultural activities, supporting services as insurance, banking etc. Planning, development and economics of tourism. Cases on tourism practices and philosophies as to past, present & future.

TRM104.title: Environment and Tourism
TRM104.description: Key global environmental problems and their impact on tourism. Positive and negative impacts of tourism on the natural and cultural environment. Analysis of the impact of alternative forms of tourism and of sustainable practices. Case studies on existing practices to review and evaluate alternative forms of tourism.

TRM107.title: Anatolian Civilisations
TRM107.description: The importance of the Anatolian cultural heritage. Races and cultures that have inhabited Anatolia. The Paleolithic and Neolithic eras in Anatolia. Chalcolithic culture and the Bronze Age. The Assyrian trading colony period. History of the Hittites and Phrygians. The culture of the Urartians. Ancient regions of Anatolia during Greek and Roman times. Istanbul through the ages. Museum and site visits.

TRM108.title: Information Systems for Tourism Industry
TRM108.description: Current developments and major issues in the field of tourism and information systems. Factors affecting the adoption and effective use of new technologies in tourism. The impact of digital technology and innovations on the tourism sector. Electronic commerce in tourism.

TRM111.title: Economics I
TRM111.description: Demand and supply, elasticity, price controls, marginal utility and indifference curve analysis, production and costs, market structures, determination of wages, return on capital.

TRM112.title: Economics II
TRM112.description: Nature of income and national income determination, employment, money and banking, fiscal and monetary policy, international trade theory and balance of payments, economic development, economic system, the general structure of Turkish economy.

TRM124.title: Business Communication
TRM124.description: Effective speech and writing traits; the importance of written communication in the changing paradigms of today's business world. Focus on types of communication with respect to mass communication and electronic media and their use in the business world. Letter and report; communicating in meetings; communication over the telephone. Lectures on communication ethics, interviews, oral presentation, listening and empathy.

TRM134.title: Principles of Management
TRM134.description: Principles of managerial practices, planning, organizing, directing and controlling, proper methods and techniques to increase managerial effectiveness and efficiency. Classical and modern approaches to management. Case histories for illustrating problems in managing organizations.

TRM141.title: Introduction to Psychology
TRM141.description: Introduction to the science of behavior including study of motivation, learning and remembering, perception, intelligence, personality, abnormal behavior and social psychology. Research methods and experimental design in psychology.

TRM151.title: Business Mathematics
TRM151.description: Basics of algebra, linear equations, inequalities, functions and graphs, systems of equations, exponential and logarithmic functions, limits and continuity, the derivative, applications of the derivative with specific examples from the service industries.

TRM153.title: Introductory Computing for Business
TRM153.description: Introduction to computer concepts in the framework of business applications. Electronic data processing. Survey of different operating systems. Mainstream package programs (word processing, databases, spreadsheets), with application practice during lab sessions.

TRM162.title: History of Civilizations
TRM162.description: Study of different civilizations from antiquity to the present. The culture produced within the framework of western civilization, with respect to art and literature. The importance of past and present civilizations in the shaping of modern thought.

TRM223.title: Accommodation Industry
TRM223.description: Introduction to the accommodation industry and its structure; review of various areas of management and hotel operations. Sales; reservations; front office; housekeeping; accounting; food and beverage; guest services; introduction to yield management systems; key performance indices and performance evaluation in hotels.

TRM224.title: Interpersonal Communication
TRM224.description: The concepts of interpersonal communication, including listening, verbal communication and nonverbal communication. Creating communication climates. Understanding “self” in interpersonal communication. Communication in groups and leadership in group communication. The effects of interpersonal communication technologies. Basic guest relations. Experimental group exercises where students get feedback from each other.

TRM231.title: Financial Accounting
TRM231.description: Introduction to accounting information system. Identifying, recording, summarising of economic transactions. Theoretical framework of accounting, generally accepted accounting principles and assumptions. Complete accounting cycle and book keeping aspects; accrual accounting, end-of-period assumptions and preparation of financial statements.

TRM232.title: Managerial Accounting for Tourism Industry
TRM232.description: Financial statements of different types of establishments in tourism industry; uniform system of accounts for hospitality industry and unique characteristics of hotel financial statements. Preparation of accounting information for managerial decision making purposes. Introduction to models and techniques for managerial decision making using accounting information; ratio analysis; funds flow statement cost-volume-profit approach; budgeting; investment analysis.

TRM241.title: Introduction to Law
TRM241.description: Social relations and law. Various legal systems, including common law, equity law and European law. Branches of law: public and private law. Sources of law. Application of law and interpretation. Rights, including the acquisition of rights and bona fides and the exercise of rights and good faith.

TRM242.title: Tourism Law
TRM242.description: Basic knowledge of legal rights and responsibilities in hotel and restaurant management. Case studies related to legal problems and the logical organization of corresponding solutions.

TRM257.title: Applied Statistics I
TRM257.description: Basic concepts of probability. The role of statistics in scientific inquiry. Organization and description of data. The logic behind the basic principles and techniques of statistical analysis. Discrete and continuous distributions. Inferences based on large samples. Sampling distributions.

TRM258.title: Applied Statistics II
TRM258.description: Introduction to statistical inference. Hypothesis testing and various inference tools such as t-tests, nonparametric two samples tests ANOVA, ANOVA for nonparametric data, crosstabulation and chi-square, correlation, simple regression, multiple regression. Practice in using statistical software.

TRM263.title: Principles of Marketing
TRM263.description: Core concepts of marketing, marketing management, marketing organizations and the marketing environment with special emphasis to services. Analysis of characteristics of the consumer and organizational markets, challenges created by the rapidly changing environmental factors, and marketing problems along with the basics of strategy formulation. Case studies in order to better involve students in the identification and the solution of the marketing problems.

TRM282.title: Travel Industry
TRM282.description: The formation of the idea of travel as an inseparable feature of modern human beings. Mobility theory; cities as spaces of tourism; historical development of transportation systems; mutual constitution of transportation, travel and tourism; social, cultural and economic impacts of transportation systems and hubs. Evolution and current workings of the travel industry; employees of travel industry; effect of technology on travel industry; current operational structure and practices; future prospects.

TRM301.title: Ancient Cities and Tourism
TRM301.description: Introduction of cultural tourism products based on historical resources. Creation of theme projects as tourism products within a historical setting, visual presentation of various theme parks. The study of history and archeology of Istanbul by slide presentations and sightseeing.

TRM307.title: Anatolian Mythologies
TRM307.description: Mythology as a source of knowledge on past civilizations. The psychological, religious and social dynamics of myths. Tools to understand mythologies. Anatolian and Near-Eastern origins of Greek myths. Refrection of myths in art.
TRM307.prerequisite: TRM 107 or consent of the instructor.

TRM313.title: Economic Issues in Tourism
TRM313.description: Economic aspects of the tourism industry. Analysis of core macro and micro economic concepts, including scarcity, opportunity cost, supply and demand, market structures, elasticity, GDP, GNP, employment, income distribution, exchange rates, balance of payments and investment decisions, all with particular focus on tourism.

TRM331.title: Management of Human Resources
TRM331.description: Functions of human resources management, including human resource planning, job analysis, job descriptions, job design, recruitment, training and development, performance appraisal, wage and salary management, job evaluation, and discipline.

TRM335.title: Introduction to Finance
TRM335.description: Techniques for determining the worth of financial assets, the trade between risk and return, financial institutions, financial analysis, financial forecasting and the optimal financial strategy.

TRM336.title: Organizational Behavior
TRM336.description: A survey of concepts and theories seeking to understand and explain individual and group behavior in organizations. Perception, motivation, leadership and group dynamics applied to the organizational settings, learning and organizational behavior modification, job attitude and satisfaction, conflict management, managing organizational change and stress.

TRM339.title: Global Institutions
TRM339.description: The global interdependence of economic, political, social, cultural, technological and ecological factors. Transnationalism, globalization and the neoliberal economy. The typology of global institutions and the role of transnational organizations in contemporary social, economic and political life. Frameworks, regulations and socio-cultural trends that animate and govern global tourism.
TRM339.prerequisite: TRM 101 or consent of the instructor.

TRM355.title: Research Methodology
TRM355.description: Hypothesis development. Research design. Univariate and multivariate data analysis methods. Qualitative research methods. Use of statistical software for data analysis.

TRM364.title: Services Marketing
TRM364.description: Management of the marketing function, with special emphasis on the requirements of service organizations. Classification of services. Integrated marketing mix for services. Issues related to the marketing of services such as service recovery and balancing demand and capacity. The role of technology in the marketing of services.

TRM366.title: Entrepreneurship and Business Planning in Tourism
TRM366.description: Theoretical framework of entrepreneurship and the role of entrepreneurs. The process of new venture development in the tourism industry. Feasibility study as a tool for new venture assessment. Basic components of a business plan, including the business concept development, assessment of industry trends and competitive structures, the preparation of marketing, management and organization plans, financial statement projections, and investment appraisal. The application of business planning and investment appraisal techniques to new venture development in tourism.

TRM373.title: Sociology of Food
TRM373.description: Analysis of the social ecology of food from an evolutionary perspective, using principles from anthropology and sociology. The relationship of food to the physiological, cultural and cognitive evolution of human beings and to other factors such as technological changes, memory and senses, health, social identity, politics, globalization and tourism.

TRM376.title: Information Systems for Hotel Industry
TRM376.description: Functions of computer reservation systems, hotel automation, front office procedures, room categories, check in and check out procedures, reservations, payment conditions and reservation cancellations, room management, rate management and hotel accounts.

TRM378.title: Food Services Management
TRM378.description: Overview of the internal workings of food services management. Food services organization structures, job descriptions, control mechanisms, systems design, and specialty food service equipment. Analysis of food services management in the context of hotels, airlines and other institutions. Field visits to various types of operations.

TRM384.title: Transportation Systems
TRM384.description: Analysis of passenger transportation systems. Historic and current developments; components, functions, demand characteristics, social and economic aspects, impact of public and international regulation; interrelationship with other tourism sectors, air transportation organization, ticketing. Models of transportation, tour operation and transportation. Importance of airline transportation in tourism; types of carriers, tickets and promotional fares; reservation procedures through computers; recent applications; passenger handling in airports and seaports.

TRM392.title: Sanitation and Hygiene
TRM392.description: The importance of sanitation in hotel operations. Food and beverage microbiology. Personal hygiene of staff. Cleanliness and maintenance of food production and service equipment and facilities. The HACCP standarts and applications.

TRM400.title: Internship
TRM400.description: Integration of the academic curriculum with practical experience in the field of tourism management. A minimum of 60 working days of supervised and structured practical experience in organizations approved by the department.

TRM402.title: Special Interest Tourism
TRM402.description: Newly emerging tourism activities that are heavily based on individual preferences and diverse life styles. Rural tourism, cultural tourism, heritage tourism, educational tourism, health tourism, senior tourism.

TRM404.title: Learning Organizations
TRM404.description: Principles and practices of learning organizations; Mental models, personal mastery, shared vision, team learning and systems thinking; Flow of knowledge, communication and building trust; Role of leadership for learning organizations; Managers as facilitators of learning; Investigation of frontiers of learning organizations; Teams work on learning organizations.
TRM404.prerequisite: Senior standing or consent of the instructor.

TRM405.title: Conventions and Special Events
TRM405.description: Event tourism, its impact on tourism economy; Trends and consumer research; destination planning and marketing; planning and marketing for individual events; convention planning and functions of convention bureaus and their impact in destinations development. Case studies on special events.

TRM406.title: Consumer Behavior
TRM406.description: Factors affecting purchase-related consumer decisions. Personal and external factors that have impact upon the consumer decision making process, attitude formation and attitude change, communication, adoptation of innovations and brand loyalty. Various views on the individual in the marketplace, and models of consumer decision making with a heavy emphasis on services. Application of consumer behavior in strategic planning of profit and nonprofit organazations and issues related to consumer trends, global markets, consumer protection and ethics in consumer behavior.
TRM406.prerequisite: TRM 263 or consent of the instructor.

TRM408.title: Operations Research for Service Industry
TRM408.description: Introduction to modeling concepts and operations research techniques as quantitative decision making tools. Topics include linear programming, duality, sensitivity analysis, transportation and assignment problems, network models and case studies from the service industries. Queuing, simulation.
TRM408.prerequisite: Senior standing or consent of the instructor.

TRM409.title: Business Ethics
TRM409.description: Introduction to professional moral values and social responsibility issues including; equal employment opportunity, discrimination prevention, service quality concerns, fair treatment of employees, employee and client privacy, honesty in public relations, post-service operations, sensitivity to community demands and attitudes.
TRM409.prerequisite: Senior standing or consent of the instructor.

TRM413.title: Tourism Destination Development
TRM413.description: Identification and evaluation of tourism resources, planning and management of tourism destination areas. Analyses of destination life cycle, approaches to destination development, interpretation of tourism trends and case examples.
TRM413.prerequisite: Senior standing or consent of the instructor.

TRM415.title: - Introduction to Professional Life
TRM415.description: Career planning; networking, and job searching strategies; assessment of changing world of work; value and process of strategic management; applications of key strategy concepts; organizational and environmental analysis.

TRM435.title: Diversity Management
TRM435.description: Place and importance of diversity management in management systems. Managerial competencies needed for diversity management. Impact of diversity management on corporate performance.
TRM435.prerequisite: TRM 336 or consent of the instructor.

TRM436.title: Corporate Consultancy
TRM436.description: Diagnosing managerial problems in companies. Problem solving process. Consultancy competencies. Ethical issues in consultancy. Consultant-client relations. Preparation and writing of the consultancy report, through internship and job-shadowing in a consulting firm.
TRM436.prerequisite: Senior standing or consent of the instructor.

TRM437.title: Airline Management I
TRM437.description: Aviation history. Micro-level commercial airline functions, civil aviation organizations, operation of airlines. Cooperation and competition in airline business; production of a seamless product. Players and their interaction in the service chain. Political, economic and social environments affecting the airline industry, legislations controlling civil aviation, air service agreements, settlement systems, distribution mechanisms, hubs and spokes, alliances. Customer loyalty programs, yield management and fleet planning.

TRM441.title: - Financial Management for Tourism and Hospitality
TRM441.description: The relationship between risk and return, calculating beta coefficients, cost of debt, cost of common stock, the weighted average cost of capital, factors that affect the weighted average cost of capital, the corporate valuation model, debt policy, payout policy, long-term financial planning, short-term financial planning, derivative instruments, international financial management, applications in the tourism and hospitality industry.

TRM465.title: Current Issues in Tourism
TRM465.description: A wide range of topics on different types and modes of travel and related travel organization systems such as adventure travel, special airport services, domestic tourism, interest travel, student and youth travel as well as corporate travel market; congress organizations; cruise market operation; group travel as well as procedures by submission and analyses of cases by specialists of the respected fields.
TRM465.prerequisite: Senior standing or consent of the instructor.

TRM468.title: Property Management and Maintenance
TRM468.description: The role of the property manager; present expenses and long term trends; leasing and contract maintenance; equipment replacement policies; planning a systems approach; staffing requirements; other related topics as waste and trash removal and disposal; security (fire, guest employer and energy saving devices); future lodging engineering systems.

TRM472.title: Business Strategy
TRM472.description: Concepts and methods for the generation, selection, implementation and evaluation of strategies. Strategic management as a process in service organizations. Overview of existing strategies through real-life examples. Application of analytical tools for strategic decision-making. Competitiveness and benchmarking. The impact of globalization, technology, and environmental concerns on strategic decisions.
TRM472.prerequisite: Senior standing or consent of the instructor.

TRM474.title: Tourism Safety and Security Management
TRM474.description: Safety and security measures and its operational procedures in air travel, cruise ships, hotels. Safety hazards, fire safety, food-borne illnesses and infection and infection diseases, medical emergencies and terrorism and the necesssary insurance selection policies as to the above hazards.

TRM476.title: Internet Marketing
TRM476.description: Inrternet as a commercial medium and its use in the tourism industry. Main areas to be covered (major topics) will include the development of the internet, social and the marketing changes brought by its utilization of the world wide web for communications, promotion, advertising and distribution.
TRM476.prerequisite: TRM 263 or consent of the instructor.

TRM492.title: Tourism Research Project
TRM492.description: Master term project preparation in a field of interest as: Tourism policy, destination marketing, culture tourism, travel agency operations, consumer preferences in tourism; cross-cultural non-verbal communication in tourism and other similar related topics.
TRM492.prerequisite: TRM 355 or consent of instructor Summer Training (Yaz Staji) The internship provides students with the oppurtunity to work within a company environment for a total of 60 workdays. INTT111.title: Economics I
INTT111.description: Basic concepts of microeconomics; demand, supply, competitive equilibrium, elasticity, price controls, the consumption decision, production and costs, technological change. Market structures. Factors of production, determination of wages and return on capital.

INTT112.title: Economics II
INTT112.description: Basic concepts of macroeconomics; the measurement and structure of national economy, productivity, output and employment. Consumption, saving, investment and the government sector. The money supply process, prices and inflation. Fiscal and monetary policies in a closed economy. Institutional determination of wages and unemployment. Business cycle analysis.

INTT121.title: Business Mathematics I
INTT121.description: Basics of algebra; functions; systems of linear algebraic equations; matrices and determinants. Limits and continuity. The derivative and its applications; curve sketching; applications to business problems.

INTT122.title: Business Mathematics II
INTT122.description: Methods of integration, applications of definite integration, area under the curve. Sequences and infinite series, tests for convergence, power series, Taylor's formula. Partial derivatives and its applications, Lagrange multipliers; applications to business problems.

INTT125.title: Information Systems For Trade
INTT125.description: Overview of information systems and data science. Inter-relationships between data, information and trade operations. Introduction to computer terminology, basic programming concepts, data types, database management methods used for acquiring, storing and transforming data. Brief review of common software and programming packages. Emerging trends in data and information technologies.

INTT132.title: Management and Organizations
INTT132.description: Principles of managerial practices, planning, organizing, directing, controlling, decision making; classical and modern approaches to management; environment and managerial culture.

INTT142.title: Legal Environment of Business
INTT142.description: Concept of law; state and constitution, state organs and their rule making powers; different legal systems; legal transactions, contracts; commercial law and companies, commercial papers; labor law. Fundamental principles of international law; international organizations; multinational corporations.

INTT162.title: Creative Thinking and Innovation
INTT162.description: Principles and approaches for improving the flexibility and originality of thinking, flourishing creativity and innovation in people and organizations. Personal thinking preferences; eliminating mental blocks; idea generation and creativity techniques; basic concepts about innovation; principles and practices for developing and managing innovations; developing an innovation strategy; the interplay between creativity, organizational processes and innovation success. Case examples and exercises to capture and implement the principles of creative thinking and innovation.

INTT203.title: Financial Accounting
INTT203.description: The accounting information system; the recording process, the trial balance, year-end adjustments, measurement of income; financial statements (income statement, balance sheet), the worksheet; detailed study of current assets (cash, receivable and inventory accounts), long lived assets; liabilities, and owners’ equity; statement of cash flow.

INTT211.title: International Trade Theories and Policies
INTT211.description: Microeconomic aspects of international economics; introduction to international economic theory and policy. Classical, neoclassical and contemporary theories of international trade; empirical evidence from real life. Comparative advantage, gains from trade. Commercial policies, tariffs, the terms of trade and income distribution, international factor movements. Regional economic issues, trade policies and their implications for advanced and developing countries including Turkey.

INTT212.title: Exchange Rate Regimes and Trade
INTT212.description: Macroeconomic aspects of international economics; the balance of payments accounting and the foreign exchange market. Exchange rate determination, exchange rate regimes, effects on imports and exports. International monetary system, global interdependence and their implications on a nation's welfare.

INTT227.title: Applied Statistics I
INTT227.description: An introduction to uses and abuses of statistics; frequency distribution, measures of central tendency and variance; basics of probability; probability distribution of discrete and continuous random variables; Binomial, Poisson, normal, exponential distributions; sampling methods and estimation; usage of computer packages in applications.

INTT228.title: Applied Statistics II
INTT228.description: Hypothesis tests, chi-square tests, analysis of variance, simple linear regression, multiple regression. Introduction to the multivariate analysis techniques; indices. Use of computer packages in applications.

INTT241.title: International Economic Law
INTT241.description: Legal aspects of international trade; international institutions regulating international trade, World Trade Organization (WTO), General Agreement of Tariffs and Trade (GATT); legal aspects of international monetary system, IMF, World Bank; balance of payments, SDR-EURO; international regulation of foreign investments; protection of foreign investments; settlement of disputes between foreign investors and states.
INTT241.prerequisite: INTT 142 or Consent of the Instructor for non INTT students.

INTT252.title: Principles of Marketing
INTT252.description: Core concepts of marketing, marketing management, marketing organizations, marketing environment and the characteristics of the consumer and organizational markets will be studied. The course will be supplemented by case studies.

INTT254.title: International Trade Operations
INTT254.description:
International trade practice, Trademap application, international sales contract, Incoterms, international trade rules (ICC), international trade documentation, international trade payment terms; collections, acceptance, letter of credit and letter of guarantees, customs clearance, international trade risks and mitigation.

INTT 277 Financial Decision Making ( 3+1+0) 3 ECTS 5

(Finansal Karar Verme)

The time value of money, interest rates, bonds and bond valuation, stocks and stock valuation, risk and return, capital budgeting decision models, cash flow estimation, the cost of capital and capital structure, capital asset pricing model, dividends and dividend policy.

INTT304.title: Managerial Accounting
INTT304.description: Cost concepts and classifications, cost-volume-profit relationships, job order costing, process costing, activity based costing and activity based management, master budget and responsibility accounting, inventory costing and capacity analysis, insourcing-outsourcing and make-or-buy decisions, bottleneck, capacity constraints, strategic profitability analysis, pricing decisions and cost management, inventory management, management control systems, multinational considerations in transfer pricing and performance measurement.

INTT321.title: Quantitative Analysis and Applications
INTT321.description: Introduction to modeling concepts and quantitative techniques as tools for decision-making. Models and applications on linear programming and sensitivity analysis, transportation, assignment, goal programming, network models; project analysis and evaluation; use of decision support software packages in applications.

INTT322.title: Operations and Supply Chain Management
INTT322.description: Designing, planning and management of the supply chain, operations, processes and activities required to transform resources into goods and services effectively. Operation flows and processes, process design, lean operations, productivity management; an integrated view of functional areas of supply chain; achieving strategic fit, planning and coordinating demand and supply, logistics, sales and operations planning, information technology and collaboration in supply chain, global supply chains.

INTT323.title: Research Methodology
INTT323.description: Quantitative and qualitative research techniques emphasizing their applications in trade; population and sampling methods, data sources, survey research, data gathering techniques, tabulation and data analysis.

INTT331.title: International Human Resource Management
INTT331.description: Institutional and cultural influences on human resource management, transfer of human resource practices in multinational companies, expatriation cycle, comparative themes, international labor relations, human resource management in North America, in Europe, in the Far East and in developing countries.

INTT333.title: International Management
INTT333.description: Analysis of cross-national differences in economic, legal-political and cultural environments; modes of foreign market entry; governmental influence on international trade and investment; internationalization strategies; international strategic alliances; organizing, leadership and control in multinational companies.

INTT334.title: Business Ethics
INTT334.description: Creating awareness and sensitivity for ethical issues. Emphasizing moral reasoning, moral behavior and moral responsibility based upon ethical principles and theories for businesses and all stakeholders. Study of ethical dilemmas and ethically controversial cases in the global business environment. Ethics-related issues of technology, corporate social responsibility, privacy, environment, marketing and consumer protection, and discrimination.

INTT341.title: International and European Union Commercial Law
INTT341.description: International law; international commercial contracts; documentation in international business transactions; payments methods; supranational integration; legal system of European Union; supremacy of the European Union law; regulatory powers of the Union organs.
INTT341.prerequisite: INTT 142 or Consent of the Instructor for non INTT students.

INTT355.title: Electronic Commerce
INTT355.description: Dynamics of the online environment in terms of strategies, trends, tools and business models. Investigation of concepts such as e-marketing channels, conversion metrics, earned and paid customer acquisition; customer lifetime value, net promoter score, customer data analytics, and user experience design through case studies and examples.

INTT358.title: Services Marketing
INTT358.description: Marketing function with special emphasis on the requirements of service organization. Application of marketing concepts, methods and techniques in the service industries. Distinctive aspects of services marketing. Marketing strategy and the marketing management process for the services exchange. The marketing mix; creating and delivering services, service quality; costs and pricing for services; communicating and promoting services; management of the customer service function; organization, implementation and control of the marketing effort. Innovative marketing strategies for services. Internationalization of services.

INTT362.title: Economic Integration and the European Union
INTT362.description: Determinants of global trade flows, patterns of industrial competition and government policies affecting international trade. The process of economic and political integration in the world and in Europe and the related economic benefits and costs. Institutional Economics of the European Community, customs union, common market and monetary union. The coordination, implementation of economic policies and enforcement of Community Law on sectors: Case studies of agriculture, manufacturing, energy, services, transportation.

INTT375.title: Risk and Insurance
INTT375.description: Definition and classifications of risk, personal and commercial risks; Techniques for managing risk, using insurance as risk transfer; Meaning and objectives of risk management, steps in risk management; Enterprise Risk Management, implementing and monitoring a risk management program; Decision Making in Financial Risk Management

INTT378.title: Trade Financing
INTT378.description: Short-term and long-term trade credits, credit risks and credit arrangements; open accounts, letters of credit, import/export drafts, bankers' acceptances, and trust receipts, understanding of the foreign exchange market, international trade and foreign exchange risks.

INTT400.title: Internship
INTT400.description: Integration of the academic curriculum with practical experience in the field of international trade. A minimum of 60 working days of supervised and structured practical experience in organizations approved by the department.

INTT402.title: Taxation in International Trade
INTT402.description: Taxation regulations and practices faced by international firms (corporate tax, income tax, value added tax and tariffs) tax refunds; tariffs in free zones; taxation in Customs Union operations; provisional importation; taxation in cross-border leasing; double taxation.

INTT410.title: Economic History of Turkey
INTT410.description: History of incentive measures for the encouragement of industry, investment and foreign exchange generating activities, foreign capital policy, the effects of these policies, history of foreign trade policy; exchange rates, tariffs, subsidies, tax refunds, the development of Turkish foreign trade, tourism policy, small business policy, development of Turkish maritime trade, importance of development plans in promoting commerce and industry.

INTT413.title: International Trade and Economic Development
INTT413.description: Process of industrial development and alternative development strategies; inward-oriented and outward-oriented development policies, their effects on exports, employment and growth. Critical analysis of Trade Liberalization policies in selected developing countries. Trade Liberalization process and growth performance from an international perspective for Turkey; import substitution policies during the 1970s, trade and exchange rate liberalization, reforms in the agricultural and state enterprise sectors. Growth prospects for the Turkish economy in the European Union and role of trade policies.

INTT414.title: Region Studies
INTT414.description: Study of the selected regions for trade strategy objectives; manpower and natural resource endowments of regions, relationships between economic structure and such economic factors as capital accumulation and level of technology, relations between economic activities and the cultural and ethnographic structure of human groups, the comparative advantages of countries and regions due to the economic strength arising from these factors, regional integration efforts and international commercial activities, rural-urban shifts.

INTT416.title: Economic History of Europe
INTT416.description: Life and the economy before the Industrial Revolution: the rise and fall of the manorial system, the prudent peasant and open fields, the growth of labor productivity in early modern English agriculture, the efficiency and distributional consequences of eighteenth century enclosures. The Industrial Revolution; demand vs. supply, the demographic transition, life in France and England, the standard of living debate and consumption. Governmental response to the Industrial Revolution; child labor and the Factory Acts, the myth of British free trade and fortress France. Industrialization beyond Great Britain; the late nineteenth century, the world economy in the twentieth century.

INTT423.title: Games and Cases in Operations Management
INTT423.description: Use of computer games for solving strategic and operational problems in business. Integration of various quantitative and qualitative techniques for developing a solution. Supported by related cases.

INTT424.title: Innovation Management: Strategies, Systems and Processes
INTT424.description: An overview of innovation as a critical tool for sustainable competitiveness in business and organizations; sources, facilitators of and barriers to innovation; total innovation management; innovation strategies, innovation process management and models; business model innovation; optimizing innovation decision making through leveraging technical and business model innovation; measurement of innovation level and performance; use of case studies and games to reinforce the concepts.

INTT425.title: International Logistics
INTT425.description: Role of international logistics in supply chains. Logistics subsystem and integrated logistics, structure of international physical distribution. International modes of transportation, packaging and security. Logistics relationships, role of logistics operators and 3PLs in the business and supply chain management. Technology and performance measurement. Interrelationships between international logistics decisions and the supply chain and other functional areas of the organization.

INTT427.title: Strategic Sourcing and Supply Management
INTT427.description: Strategic sourcing and supply management in the industrial purchasing cycle for operating supplies, raw materials, components and services. Strategic issues relating to the procurement decision process including supplier selection and evaluation, supplier management and development, supplier performance and relationship management, make-versus-buy decision, e-purchasing, purchasing law and ethics, sustainability issues, the interrelationships between purchasing and other areas of the organization and the supply chain.

INTT434.title: Business Development and Entrepreneurship
INTT434.description: Various aspects of starting, operating, and expanding the owner-managed business. Each student prepares a business plan for a new company for which financing is sought. The integration of financial planning, marketing, accounting and organizational problems in a well-written proposal for financing is emphasized.
INTT434.prerequisite: Senior standing or consent of the instructor.

INTT435.title: Strategic Management
INTT435.description: Concepts and tools for formulating and implementing strategies particularly in the context of international trade and investment; use of these tools to study the industrial environment, to predict competitive actions and to analyze how firms develop and sustain competitive advantage.

INTT438.title: International Negotiations
INTT438.description: Strategy and tactics of distributive bargaining and integrative negotiation. Emotions and cognitive biases in negotiations. Conflict resolution methods. Ethical issues in negotiations. Negotiating in different business settings, ie., personnel disputes, mergers, acquisitions, alliances, joint ventures, coalitions. Cross-cultural negotiation strategies in different regions and countries of the world. Third-party involvement in negotiations.

INTT440.title: Innovation and Technology Law
INTT440.description: Innovation and philosophy of technology law, theoretical foundations, key concepts and doctrines of intellectual property (copyrights, patents, trademarks), TRIPS Agreement, comparative analysis of the legal frameworks of international institutions concerned with intellectual property (WTO, WIPO, EU), technology transfer, trade secrets, protection of data, cybersecurity. Artificial intelligence, big data, internet of things, robots, reference case studies, case law analysis.

INTT442.title: Competition Law
INTT442.description: Introduction to the competition law, competition law in Turkey, international competition norms, EU competition law. Anti-competitive agreements, concerted practices, cartels, abuse of dominant power, merger and acquisition control, compatibility of state aid with competition rules. Case law analysis, discussions of theory and practice of the competition rules.

INTT453.title: Integrated Marketing Communications
INTT453.description: Study of communication between service suppliers and buying centers in national and international markets. Promotion in implementing marketing strategy. Promotion policy and planning; use of advertising, personal selling, publicity and sponsorship as promotion tools.

INTT454.title: Social Innovation and Impact
INTT454.description: Social innovation, social entrepreneurship, business model design for good, societal marketing, corporate social brand and its difference from corporate social responsibility, good business practices, creating a shared value, purpose vs profit trade off, conscious capitalism, social impact measurement, impact investment.

INTT457.title: Customer Behavior
INTT457.description: Buyer behavior and decision making for both consumer and organizational markets. Understanding and prediction of market place behavior and customer satisfaction. Buyer behavior principles to guide the analysis of and decision making for target markets.

INTT458.title: Digital Marketing Strategies and Community Management
INTT458.description: Digital marketing strategies, building and managing communities, online brand communities, search engine marketing, search engine optimization, content marketing, mass customization, long tail, inbound marketing, social media marketing, virality, online reputation, digital marketing return on investment.

INTT459.title: International Marketing
INTT459.description: Global marketing management. Cultural, political, economic and legal framework of international marketing. Regional market characteristics. International marketing information systems and research. Choice of international markets. Formulating international marketing strategies. Alternatives for entry and positioning, competitive analysis. International marketing mix decisions. Organization and control for international marketing operations.

INTT462.title: International Organizations
INTT462.description: The structure and activities of such international organizations as United Nations (ILO, UNESCO, ECOSOC) OECD, GATT, IMF and World Bank Group with special emphasis on the role of these organizations on international business.

INTT463.title: International Relations
INTT463.description: The evolution of the nation-state system, the operation of balance of power, deterrence, coercion, conflict, diplomacy, crisis management, and the role of international law and institutions in inter-state relations.

INTT467.title: Politics of Globalizations
INTT467.description: Analysis of the interaction between politics and the economy, and markets and political behavior in the international system. Presentation of recent developments in international political economy studies with a focus on globalization. Theoretical perspectives to analyze and critically think about various effects and challenges that a rapidly integrating world imposes on trade, finance, economic development as well as the institution of nation-states.

INTT474.title: International Financial System and Institutions
INTT474.description: The development and operation of financial markets, institutions and instruments in the world as well as Turkey; conduct of monetary policy, central banking, structure of banking industry in Turkey; competition and financial liberalization program; non-bank financial institutions and their role in the financial system; regulation and internationalization of the financial markets.

INTT480.title: International Trade Project
INTT480.description: Students work on a specific project carried out within a company environment. The topic covers a firm's understanding of a foreign market and evaluation of the feasibility of exporting or setting up a local subsidiary. The topic must be a live trade problem and must be approved by the academic advisor and company advisor.
INTT480.prerequisite: Consent of the instructor. INTT 481-489 Special Topics in International Trade (3+0+0) 3 ECTS 5 (Uluslararası Ticarette Özel Konular) An overview of the international trade education. Actual markets and high growth rate sectors are examined. Topics vary by semester and at discretion of instructor and student demand. Guest speakers from the business world help students to relate theory and practice. Each student carries out an independent study, guided by an instructor and a research project is prepared using the knowledge acquired during the previous courses. Presentation of project is also required. Consent of the instructor. SUMMER TRAINING (Yaz Stajı) The internship provides students with the opportunity to work within a company environment for a total of 70 workdays. FOREIGN LANGUAGE (Yabanci Dil) 3 Students will take a total of 18 credit hours of a second foreign language other than English for a degree in International Trade Department.
